**Your pull request section in the plan:** "04a pull request 0 — the engine fix both stacks stand on (G2, G3)". Decisions G2 and G3 in the stack-04 note are yours. Also read `docs/adr/0014-*.md` whole, `spec/multiverse/diff.md` whole (open question 7 and the same-direction rule), `spec/multiverse/propagation.md` B4–B7, and `backend/src/katalyst/domain/diff.py` and `propagation.py` (`_agreement_on`, `_states`, `_ranked_endings`, `_per_version`, `_draw`, `versions_of`, `Versions.weights`, `Versions.reweighted`).

**Files you own, and only these:** `backend/src/katalyst/domain/diff.py`; tests for it under `backend/tests/**`; `spec/multiverse/diff.md`; a dated amendment inside `docs/adr/0014-*.md` (add a dated section in place — never rewrite its existing measurements; the precedent is how record 0008 was amended); `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` **regenerated only** by `make types` (or `scripts/gen-types.sh`), never hand-edited. If the regenerated types break a frontend type-check, report it — do not edit frontend source.

**What to build.**
1. **G2 — read the direction with the same weights the number was read with.** `_agreement_on` takes the version weights. A version with no surviving world has weight zero and must not vote. Under every edit that is not an observation all weights are equal, so nothing else may move by one bit — pin that by comparing a non-observation diff with itself computed both ways, never with a typed-in number. Worlds per version stays 8; the 90% bar is untouched. Think carefully about which weights apply when only one side of the comparison carries an observation, when both do, and for a claim the observation is not evidence about (`Versions.reweighted`); state the rule once in the chapter and make the code obey that one sentence.
2. **G3 — a claim moved only by reweighting.** Observing C on the Hormuz map moves H by more than the floor while H's paired difference is exactly zero in every version (H has no causes). Keep the diff states as they are. Add **one field** on the diff's row/state for such a claim saying it moved only because the observation changed how much each version counts. Name it in plain words consistent with `spec/vocabulary.md` and the existing field names in `diff.py`, and say in the chapter exactly when it is true. The Inspector sentence (not yours to build, but quote it in the chapter word for word): *"this claim moved only because the observation made some versions count more."*
3. Tests, named as in the plan: `test_an_observation_puts_a_row_on_the_rail` · `test_a_dead_version_does_not_vote` · `test_direction_is_read_with_the_numbers_own_weights` · `test_an_edit_that_is_not_an_observation_is_unchanged_by_the_weights` · `test_a_claim_moved_only_by_reweighting_says_so`. `domain/` must stay at 100% coverage and `mypy --strict` clean.
4. `spec/multiverse/diff.md`: close open question 7 in place with what was measured and the one rule; add the reweighting paragraph; **re-measure from the engine every same-direction percentage the chapter quotes** and correct any that moved. Search the whole repo (`spec/`, `docs/`, `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `frontend/`) for any other place that quotes a number your change moved, and **list them in your report** — do not edit files you do not own.
5. The dated amendment to record 0014: what was measured (coordinator re-ran it 2026-09-17 on Hormuz, seed 20261001, `Observe(target="B", value=True)`: 209 of 2 000 versions with no surviving world; 89.05% unweighted; re-measure the weighted figure yourself and quote yours), the one rule, and that Kent chose it on 2026-09-17 over "more worlds per version".
6. Run `make types` from the repo root of your worktree and commit the regenerated `schema.ts`. Confirm `frontend` still type-checks (`cd frontend && npm ci && npm run check`).

Commit in small Conventional Commits (`adr:`, `spec:`, `fix(diff):`, `test:`, `chore(types):`). Run every verification command in the shared brief and paste their tails in your report. Hand-check your arithmetic on a tiny map of your own (three claims, one observation) and show the working in your report.

Your decisions are recorded and folded into the plans, and stack 04 is underway. Seven Opus agents are running in wave 0. Nothing is pushed yet, no pull request is open, and no model money has been spent ($0 of the $500).

## What you decided

I checked the reviewer's main measurement against the code myself before asking you. The answers are in `plans/notes/2026-09-17-kent-decisions-stack-04.md`. The stack 04 plan, `HANDOFF.md`, the roadmap, the plans README and `STATUS.md` now match them.

| Question | Your answer |
|---|---|
| Where a claim's range comes from (record 0015) | The range the model states, labelled "uncalibrated". No ensemble is built. The requirement that asked for one (FR-8) is amended. |
| "This happened" puts nothing on the change list | Count only the versions of the map that survived the observation. This is a counting fix of about ten lines, not more worlds. |
| A causeless claim moved only by reweighting | The Inspector says so in one sentence. No new diff state. |
| After the validator refuses a proposal | Up to three silent retries. You chose this over my recommendation, so record 0003 gets a dated amendment explaining why. |
| Spending ceiling | $500 for the stack, with a $15 hard stop per run written into the code. |
| When to record the examples | Hormuz as soon as the pipeline runs. All four once the prompt is frozen. |
| The eight small corrections | All eight taken as a block. |

## Two calls I took on your behalf

- **Only I run commands that spend money.** No sub-agent holds your key. The pipeline agent builds against fake responses. I record the real ones myself, and I will write the first measured cost of one map in `STATUS.md` before anything larger runs.
- **The observation fix is its own small pull request at the bottom of 04a** (`fix/04-observe-direction` → `main`). That way the join reads the new field from generated types. It makes 04a four pull requests deep, which is the limit.

## What is running

| Agent | Work |
|---|---|
| F | The observation fix in the engine, its spec chapter, and the dated amendment to record 0014 |
| W | The browser chapter on the map drawing itself |
| P1 | The proposals and grounding chapters |
| P2 | The streaming, replay and evaluation chapters |
| A | Record 0015, the amendment to record 0003, and the FR-8 wording |
| J | Joining the canvas to the engine (needs no model) |
| M | The model pipeline, built against fake responses; it stops for my review before the stream |

As each agent reports, I run its tests and lints myself, check its diff against the files it owns, and launch the app to look. For the chapters, I then put a read-only reviewer over all six, commit for the writers, push, and open the pull requests. I will tell you as each one opens.

> - **FR-8 (P1)** Ensemble: N independent generations reconciled into one graph; run-to-run disagreement surfaces as link *agreement* — a number computed from how far the independent runs differed, never a self-report by the model.

### FR-8, after

> - **FR-8 (P1)** Where a claim's starting number and range come from: **the likelihood and range the model stated in its proposal**, stamped as a `model` belief by us, shown under the label *model interval, uncalibrated*, and never merged with a user's or a market's number (amended 2026-09-17; decision record 0015). **No ensemble in v1**: no claim is asked about twice, no map is generated several times over, and **two maps are never reconciled into one** — `spec/multiverse/diff.md` anti-pattern 4, *do not infer a difference by matching two maps*, is the warrant. A **measured run-to-run number** — how far independent generations differed about a claim, computed and never self-reported — is deferred, and the word *agreement* is kept free on screen for the day one exists. # ADR-0015: A claim starts with the range the model stated, labelled as stated — not yet an ensemble

## Context and Problem Statement

Every claim on a generated map arrives with three numbers from the model: a likelihood and the two ends of a range around it — `.35 (.20–.49)`. Record 0014 settled what those numbers **mean**: the two ends are the 10th and 90th percentiles of the likelihood itself, so the range says *how sure we are of the number*, not *how much the world can move*. It did not settle where the three numbers **come from**, and said so in its section G: *"Whether a claim's starting range should come from measured disagreement across several independent model runs. Kent: decide in stack 04."*

The pull of the question is real. Record 0014 collected published evidence, as input rather than as a decision, that ranges a language model states about itself are reliably too narrow. The alternative on offer is to ask the same question several times and read the spread of the answers as the range — a measurement instead of a self-report, which is the rule this repository applies everywhere else. `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` FR-8 had already written that alternative down as a requirement, in the strongest possible form: *N* independent generations of the whole map, reconciled into one.

94:## Amendment (2026-09-17)
95-
96-**Rule 2's single targeted re-prompt becomes up to three fresh proposals, none of them told why the last was refused.** Kent decided this on 2026-09-17, before any of the pipeline was written. When `domain.validate` rejects a proposal, `engine/` asks the model again for **the same claim on the frontier** — the claim it was trying to expand — and the next call is **not** told what was wrong. Thr
97-
98-**The reason, and it is the whole reason: violation text never enters a prompt.** A prompt that names the violations asks the model to get past our checker. What we want is a claim that is *right*; passing the checker is meant to be a consequence of that, not a substitute for it. The two come apart in the ordinary case — told "this claim has no resolution criteria", a model will write criteria 
99-
100-**Said honestly: the design review recommended keeping this record's original rule** — re-ask once, naming the violations — because it converges in fewer calls and wastes less money on attempts that repeat the same mistake. Kent chose the silent retries anyway, for the reason above. The cost is real and is accepted: some refusals will repeat.
101-
102-**What has not changed.** The decision itself — the domain layer owns validity, the model proposes, a broken proposal is rejected with its **full** list of violations and is never silently patched up. The retry is still bounded (three attempts, not an unbounded repair loop) and still logged, and a claim that never passes still surfaces as a proper state — the claim closes, the stream says so —
103-
104-**One older wording, noted rather than repaired.** Rule 2 says `engine/` receives a `GraphProposal` — the shape the model fills. ADR-0006 (2026-09-16) later settled that one call returns **one** proposal — a claim plus its incoming arrow, or a typed `Stop` — in a model it calls `Proposal`, and **neither record says in so many words that the later shape replaces the earlier name.** It does: no 
105-
106-Amended in place rather than superseded, because nothing in the decision changed: one bound on retrying was replaced by another, inside the same rule.
**Agreement.** The share of versions of the map in which a change moved the same way. Computed, never self-reported. A claim counts as `shifted` when it moved by .005 or more **and** agreement is at least 90%; agreement is then shown as its own column beside the change, never multiplied into the ranking. **On screen that column is headed *same direction*** (decided 2026-09-17), and the width column beside it is headed *how firm*; the field names stay `agreement` and `range_width`. Keeping the word *agreement* off this screen leaves it free for stack 04's run-to-run number. Stack 04 may compute a second agreement number — how far several independent generation runs agreed on a claim's likelihood (decision record 0014 defers that question). Same idea, same rule; wherever both could be meant, say which.
What the model-facing pipeline is allowed to do about a rejection is a different question, and not this chapter's: `engine/` may issue **one** targeted re-prompt that names the violations and asks for a corrected proposal, bounded and logged; a second failure surfaces as a proper error state, not a spinner (decision record 0003, rule 2). That loop, its bounds, and what the user sees while it runs belong to [`../generation/`](../generation/) and are written in stack 04. `domain/` knows nothing about it. `validate` returns a list and has no opinion about what anyone does next.
   **Decided 2026-09-17:** the second option — `confidence` is dropped for version 1, and the field is gone from the model above. Four reasons, in order of weight. Nothing consumed it: no invariant named it, no code read it, and the canvas gives its where-did-this-come-from encoding to `provenance`, not to this (UX-6 in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §7). It was a self-report by the one component we have already decided not to trust to declare its own quality — the same argument that keeps the model's hands off `provenance` (decision record 0003, rule 5). It cost a third elicited item on every link, against decision record 0005's deliberate budget of one number and one sentence per arrow. And `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` FR-8 already uses the word "confidence" for something else entirely: run-to-run *agreement* across independent generations, which is computed, not claimed. What the field claimed to carry is carried by `provenance`, the rationale sentence and the range on the belief. If stack 04's ensemble wants to show how much the independent runs disagreed about an arrow, it adds a computed `agreement` field — a receipt, not a self-report. No decision record was needed: decision record 0005's table of link fields never listed `confidence`.

It did not settle where the three numbers **come from**, and said so in its section G: *"Whether a claim's starting range should come from measured disagreement across several independent model runs. Kent: decide in stack 04."*

The pull of the question is real. Record 0014 collected published evidence, as input rather than as a decision, that ranges a language model states about itself are reliably too narrow. The alternative on offer is to ask the same question several times and read the spread of the answers as the range — a measurement instead of a self-report, which is the rule this repository applies everywhere else. `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` FR-8 had already written that alternative down as a requirement, in the strongest possible form: *N* independent generations of the whole map, reconciled into one.

94:## Amendment (2026-09-17)
95-
96-**Rule 2's single targeted re-prompt becomes up to three fresh proposals, none of them told why the last was refused.** Kent decided this on 2026-09-17, before any of the pipeline was written. When `domain.validate` rejects a proposal, `engine/` asks the model again for **the same claim on the frontier** — the claim it was trying to expand — and the next call is **not** told what was wrong. Thr
97-
98-**The reason, and it is the whole reason: violation text never enters a prompt.** A prompt that names the violations asks the model to get past our checker. What we want is a claim that is *right*; passing the checker is meant to be a consequence of that, not a substitute for it. The two come apart in the ordinary case — told "this claim has no resolution criteria", a model will write criteria 
99-
100-**Said honestly: the design review recommended keeping this record's original rule** — re-ask once, naming the violations — because it converges in fewer calls and wastes less money on attempts that repeat the same mistake. Kent chose the silent retries anyway, for the reason above. The cost is real and is accepted: some refusals will repeat.
101-
102-**What has not changed.** The decision itself — the domain layer owns validity, the model proposes, a broken proposal is rejected with its **full** list of violations and is never silently patched up. The retry is still bounded (three attempts, not an unbounded repair loop) and still logged, and a claim that never passes still surfaces as a proper state — the claim closes, the stream says so —
103-
104-**One older wording, noted rather than repaired.** Rule 2 says `engine/` receives a `GraphProposal` — the shape the model fills. ADR-0006 (2026-09-16) later settled that one call returns **one** proposal — a claim plus its incoming arrow, or a typed `Stop` — in a model it calls `Proposal`, and **neither record says in so many words that the later shape replaces the earlier name.** It does: no 
105-
106-Amended in place rather than superseded, because nothing in the decision changed: one bound on retrying was replaced by another, inside the same rule.
**Agreement.** The share of versions of the map in which a change moved the same way. Computed, never self-reported. A claim counts as `shifted` when it moved by .005 or more **and** agreement is at least 90%; agreement is then shown as its own column beside the change, never multiplied into the ranking. **On screen that column is headed *same direction*** (decided 2026-09-17), and the width column beside it is headed *how firm*; the field names stay `agreement` and `range_width`. Keeping the word *agreement* off this screen leaves it free for stack 04's run-to-run number. Stack 04 may compute a second agreement number — how far several independent generation runs agreed on a claim's likelihood (decision record 0014 defers that question). Same idea, same rule; wherever both could be meant, say which.
What the model-facing pipeline is allowed to do about a rejection is a different question, and not this chapter's: `engine/` may issue **one** targeted re-prompt that names the violations and asks for a corrected proposal, bounded and logged; a second failure surfaces as a proper error state, not a spinner (decision record 0003, rule 2). That loop, its bounds, and what the user sees while it runs belong to [`../generation/`](../generation/) and are written in stack 04. `domain/` knows nothing about it. `validate` returns a list and has no opinion about what anyone does next.
   **Decided 2026-09-17:** the second option — `confidence` is dropped for version 1, and the field is gone from the model above. Four reasons, in order of weight. Nothing consumed it: no invariant named it, no code read it, and the canvas gives its where-did-this-come-from encoding to `provenance`, not to this (UX-6 in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §7). It was a self-report by the one component we have already decided not to trust to declare its own quality — the same argument that keeps the model's hands off `provenance` (decision record 0003, rule 5). It cost a third elicited item on every link, against decision record 0005's deliberate budget of one number and one sentence per arrow. And `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` FR-8 already uses the word "confidence" for something else entirely: run-to-run *agreement* across independent generations, which is computed, not claimed. What the field claimed to carry is carried by `provenance`, the rationale sentence and the range on the belief. If stack 04's ensemble wants to show how much the independent runs disagreed about an arrow, it adds a computed `agreement` field — a receipt, not a self-report. No decision record was needed: decision record 0005's table of link fields never listed `confidence`.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

content.text:
P1 has finished `proposals.md` and `grounding.md`. Its two cross-chapter corrections have been sent to P2 and M while they are still working. Their messages are queued for delivery at their next tool round.

- **The `search_cap` stop reason is gone.** Reaching the search cap stops searching, not the generation. Later arrows simply come out `argued`, so nothing could ever choose that value. P1's own `proposals.md` still lists it, with a note that nothing can choose it, as an open question. I'll remove it there in the review round.
- **A new `StartingClaim` shape.** The hypothesis and the Verify destination have no cause, so they cannot be ordinary proposals. It is asked once, outside the proposal union. I judged this a real gap in the plan, not a preference.

P1 also found something you should know. **On a generated map, no arrow can ever be marked `asserted`.** Every arrow must carry a rationale, and our code writes the provenance before validation. So an accepted arrow is always `documented` or `argued`.

The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths (record 0014) will therefore see only two of its seven widths on any generated map: `documented` at 0.15 and `argued` at 0.40. I think that is still honest, since "well-backed" against "merely argued" is exactly the distinction you wanted visible. I'll make sure agent X says so plainly when it builds the spread. Nothing to decide now.

F, W, P2, J and M are still running. A and P1 are waiting for P2, since they share a worktree. After P2 I run the read-only reviewer over all six chapters, commit, and open the pull request.

## Open questions

*Raised 2026-09-17, when this chapter was written.*

1. **`done.reason` carries `search_cap`, and nothing chooses it.** Under [`grounding.md`](grounding.md)'s rule, reaching the searches cap turns searching off and the generation carries on, so no run can end for that reason. Either the value goes, or the cap ends the run. **Recommendation: drop the value** in the pull request that writes `engine/events.py`, because a reason nobody can produce is a reason a reader will one day trust. [`streaming.md`](streaming.md) carries the event vocabulary and would carry the change.
2. **Does the vendor's structured-output call take a discriminated union directly?** `Proposal` is a union of three shapes, and a structured-output format may want a single object at the top. If it does, the union is wrapped in a one-field object and nothing else changes — no field is renamed and no behaviour moves. Verified against the `claude-api` skill in the pipeline pull request, not guessed here.
3. **Should a vendor refusal and a malformed answer carry codes of their own?** Today both arrive as a `Refused` with an empty violation list and a plain sentence, so a reader cannot tell *the model declined* from *the answer did not parse* except by reading the sentence. Such a code would live in `engine/`, not in `domain/validity.py`, because neither is a fault in a map — the nineteen codes there stay nineteen.
4. **A generated map can hold no feedback arrow.** `LinkDraft` has no `reflexive` field, so the one kind of arrow allowed to close a loop cannot be proposed, and a proposal that closes a loop is always refused. The shipped example has one such arrow, hand-written. Add the field in stack 06, when unrolling a feedback arrow over time actually does something?
5. **Which day a generated claim's resolve-by date is checked against.** `validate` reads no clock, so a model that writes a date already past is not caught by the map's rules. `engine/` can see today. Is a stale date a violation, a warning on the world, or nothing? This is [`../graph/proposition.md`](../graph/proposition.md) Open questions 4, still open, and generation is the first caller that could answer it.

<result>All verification is green and the tree is clean. Here is my report.

---

## What I built

**G2 — the direction is read with the same weights the number was read with.** `backend/src/katalyst/domain/diff.py` gains `_counting_for(behind_a, behind_b, claim_id)`, which works out how much each version of the map counts when one claim's move is read, and `_agreement_on` now takes that vector. The rule is one sentence: **a version counts for the move by as much as it counted for the two numbers — the smaller of the two weights it carried — so a version with no surviving world counts for nothing and does not vote.** The three cases the brief asked about fall out of that sentence with no special-casing: only world B observed → world B's weights; both observed → the smaller of the two; a claim the observation is not evidence about (not in `Versions.reweighted`) → every version counts 1, on both sides. If nothing survived anywhere, every version counts the same again — mirroring `_band`'s own fallback in the same corner, so the number and its direction stay read the same way.

**G3 — a claim moved only by reweighting.** `ClaimDiff` gains one field, `moved_only_by_reweighting: bool`. It is true exactly when the claim is in both worlds, it moved by at least `0.005`, and **not one version that counts** moved at all (every paired difference among them is exactly zero). The four states are untouched. Only an observation can set it: under every other edit both worlds count every version the same, so identical version-by-version answers give an identical number and the move is exactly nothing. It lives on `ClaimDiff` and not on `DeltaRow`, because such a claim's same-direction share is zero by construction and so can never be `shifted` and never reach the rail — the chapter says that.

Note the subtlety the brief's wording nearly hides: **"every paired difference is zero" is false for the dead versions.** A version with no surviving world reports `0` rather than the prior (`_per_version`'s `safe` divisor), so H's paired difference is `−prior` in exactly those 209 versions. The condition is over the versions that *count*.

**The measured effect**, Hormuz, seed `20261001`, 2 000 × 8, `Observe(target="B", value=True)`:

| | before the fix | after |
|---|---|---|
| Versions with no surviving world | 209 of 2 000 | same (that is the input, not the bug) |
| M1, M2 same-direction share | `89.05%` | `98.66%` (`99.44%` among survivors, one vote each) |
| States | both `unchanged` | both `shifted` |
| The rail | empty; second summary sentence | M1 `+.21` on 2026-10-02 at 100%, M2 `+.16` on 2026-10-04 at 100%; first summary sentence |

`Observe(target="C", value=True)` moves H `.3558 → .3647` (`.356 → .365`, exactly Kent's figures), `moved_only_by_reweighting` true, state still `unchanged`, `agreement` exactly `0.0`.

**Chapter, record, tests, types.** `spec/multiverse/diff.md`: open question 7 closed in place with what was measured and with both G2 and G3; the rule stated once in B3 under its own heading plus the reweighting paragraph quoting the Inspector sentence word for word; the data model gains the field with the exact condition; B4 gains the rail an observation now produces; two anti-patterns (7 and 8, pushing the old 7 to 9) and three invariants, `INV-multiverse.31`–`.33`. `docs/adr/0014`: a dated `## Amendment (2026-09-17)` at the end, in record 0008's style, plus one forward-pointing line under the title; every existing measurement left exactly as taken. Five tests as named in the plan. `schema.ts` regenerated by `make types` only, and idempotent on a second run.

## Hand-check, on a tiny map of my own

Three claims, one observation, a budget small enough to add up: `top` (hypothesis, **no causes**, `.40 (.25–.55)`) → `seen` (`.12 (.03–.35)`, +1.0 step) and → `far` (market, `.30 (.20–.45)`, +0.4 step). `observe(seen, true)`, 6 versions × 4 worlds, seed `20261001`. The engine's per-version weights come back `[0, ¼, ¼, 0, ¼, ¾]` — versions 1 and 4 lost all four worlds. Total weight = `1.50`.

**`seen`** — paired differences `[−.038, +.803, +.845, −.077, +.650, +.295]`, move `+.746`. Versions 2, 3, 5, 6 agree.
· one vote each: `4/6 = 66.67%` · weighted: `(¼+¼+¼+¾)/1.50 = 1.50/1.50 = 100.00%` · **engine: 100.00%** ✓
Versions 1 and 4 "voted against" only because a version with no surviving world reports `0`.

**`far`** — paired differences `[−.307, +.039, +.048, −.231, +.050, −.008]`, move `+.062`. Versions 2, 3, 5 agree.
· one vote each: `3/6 = 50.00%` · weighted: `(¼+¼+¼)/1.50 = 0.75/1.50 = 50.00%` · **engine: 50.00%** ✓ — the weights do not always change the answer, which is the honest half of the story.

**`top`** (no causes) — per version, base: `[.328683, .399031, .408370, .265285, .477988, .661118]`; after: `[0, .399031, .408370, 0, .477988, .661118]`. Among the four versions that count the paired difference is exactly `0`.
· base number `= 2.540475 / 6 = 0.423413` — **engine: 0.423413** ✓
· after number `= [¼(.399031+.408370+.477988) + ¾(.661118)] / 1.50 = [.321347 + .495839] / 1.50 = .817186 / 1.50 = 0.544791` — **engine: 0.544791** ✓
· move `+0.121378 ≥ 0.005`, no counting version moved → **`moved_only_by_reweighting = True`, `agreement = 0.0`, state `unchanged`** ✓
The same six version numbers, counted two ways, are the whole move. That is the field's definition, arithmetic.

## Where I deviated from the plan, and why

- **The two-sided rule is the *smaller* of the two weights.** The plan states the rule for the case that matters (world A unweighted), where any combination rule degenerates to world B's weights; it does not say what happens when both sides observe something. I took `min`, because "the same weights the number was read with" has no single referent when there are two readings, and "a version can only speak about a difference as far as it counted in *both* numbers" is the one sentence that covers all three cases without an exception. A product would also work; `min` is the honest bound, is exact whenever one side is unweighted, and gives the "nothing else moves" guarantee for free.
- **The G3 condition is "no version *that counts* moved", not "every version".** Forced by the measurement above; the plan's wording would have made the field false on the very claim it was written for.
- **Three invariants and two anti-patterns added, not asked for.** The chapter's INVARIANTS section promises that every statement names the test that checks it; five new tests with nothing to point at would have made the chapter untrue. This renumbers diff.md's anti-patterns 7 → 9; nothing anywhere in the repo cites diff.md's anti-patterns by number (checked).
- **No screenshots of new states, because there are none.** This pull request changes no pixel: the canvas reads the stored example and is not joined to the engine yet, and the Inspector sentence is 04a's later pull requests. I ran the app anyway at 1600 × 1000 against the regenerated types — launchpad and the Hormuz map both draw identically, **zero console errors** — plus the real end-to-end test in chromium, which passes.
- **`docs/adr/README.md` not touched.** Record 0008's row reads "(amended 2026-09-17)"; 0014's should too. It is outside my grant (which is the amendment *inside* `0014-*.md`) and `docs/adr/**` belongs to 04b.

## Which chapter numbers my change made stale

**None in `diff.md`.** I re-measured from the engine every same-direction percentage the chapter quotes, at seed `20261001` and the shipped budget, and **not one moved** — as predicted, because no edit but an observation weights anything:

| Where | Quoted | Re-measured |
|---|---|---|
| B3, anti-pattern 1, `do(H)` → B | `99.9%` | `99.85%` ✓ |
| B4 rail, strike branch, M1 / M2 / N1 | `96.5%` / `95.5%` / `99.9%` | `96.55%` / `95.50%` / `99.85%` ✓ |
| B2, strike branch, "every one clears the 90% bar" | — | B `94.15`, C `100`, H `100`, M1 `96.55`, M2 `95.50`, N1 `99.85` ✓ |
| OQ7, `observe(B)` moves M1 / M2 | `+.063` / `+.107` | `+.0626` / `+.1066` ✓ |
| OQ7, `observe(B)` moves H | `−0.0002` | `−0.00019` ✓ |
| OQ7, M1 and M2 same-direction share | `89%` | `89.05%` unweighted → **`98.66%` weighted** — the one number that moved, and it is the question being closed |

**Stale elsewhere — files I do not own and did not edit.** Please route these:

| File | What is stale | Likely owner |
|---|---|---|
| `spec/multiverse/propagation.md:323` | points at "`diff.md`'s open question 7 … and the two candidate repairs". It is closed, and neither repair was taken. Its `−0.0002` figure is still correct | unassigned in the 04a/04b split — coordinator |
| `spec/vocabulary.md:48` (**Agreement**), `:44` (**Diff**), `:73` (**Delta rail**) | "the share of versions of the map" wants "of the versions that count"; **Diff** could name the new field | — |
| `spec/workbench/diff-view.md:124` | the browser's `ClaimDiff` shape needs `moved_only_by_reweighting` | **04a pull request 1** |
| `spec/workbench/diff-view.md:260` | the **same direction** column's one-line answer | 04a pull request 1 |
| `spec/workbench/inspector.md` | the G3 sentence, word for word: *"this claim moved only because the observation made some versions count more."* | 04a pull request 1 |
| `frontend/src/world/types.ts:562`, `frontend/src/graph/diff/endings.ts:23` | the hand-written diff row type and the column's description | **04a pull request 2** (the join) |
| `docs/adr/README.md:22` | 0014's row should read "(amended 2026-09-17)", as 0008's does | 04b |
| `README.md:111`, `ARCHITECTURE.md:177,180` | "**259** server tests" — it is now **264**. 177 browser tests is unchanged | 04b's top pull request |

## Open questions

1. **Two observed worlds compared to each other.** `min` is my call, argued above, not Kent's. Nothing in the product can reach it yet (the diff route builds world A from a branch too, so it is reachable the day two observation branches are compared). If Kent prefers the product, it is one line and the chapter's one sentence changes with it.
2. **`moved_only_by_reweighting` is a plain `bool`, not `bool | None`,** where `agreement` beside it is `float | None`. A statement about a move that did not happen is simply not true, and a plain boolean is kinder to the browser. Flagging the asymmetry.
3. **`test_an_edit_that_is_not_an_observation_is_unchanged_by_the_weights` replaces `_counting_for` for the duration of one call.** That is the only honest reading of "compare a non-observation diff with itself computed both ways" now that the old code path is gone — doctoring the `Versions` instead would be trivially true, since a non-observation world's weights are already all one.
4. **`domain/` coverage was already at 100% before my extra corner test**, because a randomly generated branch occasionally drives an observation to total extinction. I pinned that corner deterministically inside `test_a_dead_version_does_not_vote` rather than leaving 100% to a hypothesis draw.

Exit code 1
### B4 — how a generation ends, and the one reason it gives

A claim of kind `market` or `not_tradeable` is an **ending**: there is nothing downstream of a trade, so an ending never joins the frontier. A generation stops when the frontier is **empty** — every line closed, whether by an ending, by a `Stop`, by a cap, or by three refusals in a row.

The stream ends with one `done` event carrying **one** of seven reasons. **The rule: the reason names what closed the last claim that was still open**, with two overrides above it. One rule, so two readers cannot get two answers.

| # | `done.reason` | Chosen when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `spend_cap` | **Override.** The running receipt reached the run's spending cap. Checked after every call, so nothing further is asked |
| 2 | `no_terminal` | **Override.** The map ends nowhere you can act on, even after the last ending-seeking call (B6) |
| 3 | `depth_cap` · `width_cap` · `claim_cap` | The last open claim was closed by that cap: it sat at the depth cap, it already had its full width of children, or the map was full |
| 4 | `model_stopped` | The last open claim was closed because three proposals in a row for it were refused — the map is finished, and one line was abandoned rather than ended |
| 5 | `reached_terminal` | The last open claim answered `Stop`, or the claim it produced was an ending. The ordinary, good ending |

There is no `search_cap`. Reaching the searches cap stops **searching**, not the generation ([`grounding.md`](grounding.md) B6), so it can never be what closed a claim.

`done.reason` never carries `no_path` either. Whether a Verify run found a path is a fact about the *path*, reported once on the `verdict` event and nowhere else — two derivations of one line eventually disagree (Kent, 2026-09-17).

#### The worked run, step by step

One Hormuz generation through the Explore door, at the default caps: depth 5, width 3, 30 claims. `at` is the position in the transcript, from 0. The browser chapter draws this exact run, so nothing here is approximate.

> **Then how does the replay badge appear at the start, when `mode` arrives at the end?**
> It does not come from the stream. The first screen already asked `GET /api/readyz`, which reports `model_key_present`, never the key itself, and — settled 2026-09-17 — **`replayable`, the examples that can be played and the day each was recorded**. So before the first keystroke the screen knows whether anything it runs will be a replay, and knows the date record 0012's sentence has to print. The receipt's `mode` is

### The seven reasons a generation stops

`Done.reason` has seven values and each says a different true thing. The rules that produce them belong to [`proposals.md`](proposals.md); this is the vocabulary.

| Reason | What happened |
|---|---|
| `reached_terminal` | Every open claim closed and the map ends in at least one `market` or `not_tradeable` claim (INV-9 — every map ends in something you could trade, or an explicit statement that you could not). The ordinary, good ending |
| `depth_cap` | The map grew as many layers from the hypothesis as the run allowed |
| `width_cap` | A claim was given as many children as the run allowed |
| `claim_cap` | The map reached as many claims in total as the run allowed |
| `spend_cap` | The running receipt reached the run's spending cap (Kent, G5). `Failed` is not used: stopping on budget is a decision, not a fault |
| `model_stopped` | A line closed short — the model answered `Stop`, or three proposals in a row were refused — with no cap tripped |
| `no_terminal` | The map ends nowhere anybody could act on, even after the one last ending-seeking call per open claim, and the stream says so rather than inventing one |

**There is deliberately no `search_cap`.** The searches-per-generation cap (Kent, S2) stops the *searching*, not the generation: past the cap, calls stop declaring the search tool and later arrows come back `argued` instead of `documented`, and the run carries on to a proper ending. A complete map with some unbacked arrows is a better answer than a truncated one, and the origin marks on the wires say which arrows are

**Two dated amendments, in place.** Record 0003, rule 2: after a refusal, up to three fresh proposals for the same claim, **none told why the last was refused** — violation text never enters a prompt, so a prompt can never steer the model toward passing the validator rather than being right. The amendment says plainly that the design review recommended the original rule and Kent chose otherwise. Record 0006: `documented` needs a source the search tool itself returned in that call, and an arrow that finds nothing is `argued` — no generated arrow is ever `asserted`.

**The chapters** (`spec/generation/`):

| Chapter | Settles |
|---|---|
| `proposals.md` | The proposal shapes — the model is structurally unable to mint an identifier, declare provenance, or return two things; accept and mint, or refuse with every reason; the caps; one rule for why a generation stopped; the Verify door and an honest `no_path`; **one worked Hormuz run, step by step** |
| `grounding.md` | Search at generation time; provenance written by us from what the search returned; base rates before the inside view; what happens at the search cap |

| `evaluation.md` | The recorded-response layer; four structure-only cases; **the scorecard's fields named now**, so a later critique pass or ensemble has a baseline |

INV-13 (continuous integration runs with no model API key; the model boundary is exercised only through recorded responses) — the chapters say how. INV-1, INV-2, INV-9 (every claim says how it will be checked; every arrow gives its reason; every map ends in something you could trade or an explicit statement that you could not) — guaranteed by our validator, never asked of the model. - **FR-9's critique pass** — out of this stack: it doubles the calls and its value cannot be read until the scorecard exists.
- No code. No pastcast (stack 07). No storage (stack 05).
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the PRD's NFR-7 and FR-28 wording — swept in the top pull request of this stack.

Confirmed by inspecting the installed SDK's own signatures and types, not from memory.

**Four things the skill adds or says differently:**

1. **The skill's "`output_format` is deprecated" warning applies to `messages.create()`, not to `messages.parse()`** — whose signature takes `output_format` and merges it into `output_config.format` itself. Record 0006's review item ("no `output_config={"format": …}` dicts alongside `output_format=Model`") is right; worth one sentence in the record so nobody "fixes" it later.
2. **The skill says to enable server-side `fallbacks` by default on `claude-opus-5`.** Record 0006 explicitly declines it ("a refusal here should be seen, not hidden"). I followed the record. **For Kent.**
3. `temperature`/`top_p`/`budget_tokens` are not merely discouraged on Opus 5 — they return a 400.
4. `anthropic` 1.x is built on **`httpx2`**, not `httpx`. I checked `vcr/patch.py`: vcrpy 8.3.0 patches `httpx2` transports, so cassettes will work. Worth knowing if vcrpy is ever pinned back.

**The citations tension, resolved from the skill.** Structured output is incompatible with `citations: {enabled: true}` on **document** blocks (400). Web search is a different mechanism: its results arrive as their own `web_search_tool_result` content blocks *alongside* the structured text block. `WebSearchToolResultBlock.content` is either a `list[WebSearchResultBlock]` (`url`, `title`, `page_age`, `encrypted_content`) or a single `WebSearchToolResultError` — so a failed search reads as nothing found rather than raising. `found_in` reads those blocks and nothing else, which is S1's set exactly. We declare no document blocks anywhere, so the incompatibility never arises.

- **`Outcome` gained `calls` and `cache_write_tokens`; `Receipt` gained `cache_write_tokens`.** Cache writes cost *more* than a fresh token and a run pays them on its first call; a paused answer costs two round trips. A ceiling checked against a number smaller than the truth is not a ceiling. (`Receipt.searches` was already there and the coordinator confirmed it.)
- **`Outcome` has both `about` (the claim the call asked about) and `frontier` (what is still open after folding).** The shapes sheet's `frontier` is the second; a refusal also needs the first to be traceable back to its question.
- **The width cap counts arrows leaving a claim, not claims caused** — otherwise a run could propose arrows for ever. This is what `proposals.md` B4's step 4 actually does.
- **The ending-seeking pass runs after the claim cap too** (B6 says to) and may take the map one claim past it. Only the money stops it. Tested.
- **One known gap, stated in a comment where it lives:** an answer that does not fit the shape raises inside the client library, so that call's counters never reach us. The round trip is counted; its tokens are left at nothing, because nothing is what we know. One call in a run of dozens.
- **`no_path`'s `nearest` has two branches.** When something on the map touches the destination it is a real distance (fewest arrows, walked either way). When nothing does — the common case, since a destination arrives with no arrows — "closest" has no meaning, so the verdict names how far the story *did* get and the sentence says which of the two it is. `proposals.md` B7 assumes a nearest always exists; both branches are computed, neither is invented.
- **`found_in`/`keep_cited`/`provenance_of` live in `expand.py`**, since `engine/grounding.py` is not in my owned files.

- **Coordinator item 6 (optional `seed`, minted by `engine/ids.py`) is left for the stream pull request** — minting it belongs to the route that starts a generation, and `engine/ids.py` is not in this pull request's files.

## Disagreements I found (plan / chapters / mechanics)

1. **`grounding.md` B6: "later calls declare no search tool at all."** Changing the tool list is the one change that invalidates the *entire* prompt cache — tools render before everything. I followed the chapter and wrote the cost into `client.py`: one full-price call at the switch, in a run of dozens. **`tool_choice: {"type": "none"}` would give the identical observable behaviour at no cost** (the skill's invalidation table: a `tool_choice` change leaves the tools and system caches intact). Worth reopening in one line; INV-generation.12 currently pins the expensive form.
2. **`grounding.md` calls `max_uses` "an argument, not a constant."** In my code it is a module constant, because a per-call value that counted down would rewrite the front of every request. It is fixed per run and changed in one place. The chapter's intent is met; its wording is not.
3. **`proposals.md` B4 row 5** says `reached_terminal` is chosen when the last open claim answered `Stop` "**or the claim it produced was an ending**". 1. **`backend/src/katalyst/engine/__init__.py`** still says *"The layer may re-ask the model once, naming the reasons; a second failure becomes a visible error rather than a spinner."* That is the pre-G4 rule and contradicts record 0003's dated amendment. It will bite continuous integration one day — the strategy should draw priors away from the denormal floor, or the `assume` needs a real margin. Agent F's or the coordinator's call.

**None.** I quoted no measured number and changed no fixture or engine rule that a chapter quotes. The two numbers this pull request carries — the searches cap of 30 and one search per call — both come from the chapters, not from me.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=… make record-cassettes
```

It runs `pytest tests/boundary -m "not handmade" --record-mode=rewrite`, then re-runs `test_no_cassette_contains_a_key` **with the key unset** to prove the stripping worked.

It records four tests = **five model calls** (`test_generation_receipt_records_cache_reads` makes two), each allowed **one** web search. On the table in `engine/pricing.py` that is well under a dollar — the true figure is a measurement for `STATUS.md`, not a guess.

The other four cassettes cannot be recorded live and are marked `handmade`, so `record-cassettes` leaves them alone. Each test's docstring names the exact edit: take a recorded body and replace the proposal with a `B → H` link (cycle), blank `resolution.criteria`, add a citation the search never returned, or replace every citation with one it never returned. A new `handmade` pytest marker is registered in `pyproject.toml` (`--strict-markers` is on).

`tests/boundary/conftest.py` adds **body matching** to the shared recorder settings (asking for the parent fixture rather than repeating the key-stripping), and `decode_compressed_response` so a person and a secret scanner can read a recording.

## Verified against the `claude-api` skill (read 2026-09-17)

Record 0006 holds up on every specific: `anthropic` SDK · `claude-opus-5` (exact string, never date-suffixed) · `thinking={"type":"adaptive"}` · `client.messages.parse(output_format=Model)` → `.parsed_output` · `web_search_20260209` with `max_uses` · `cache_control={"type":"ephemeral"}` on the first system block · `stop_reason == "refusal"` with `stop_details` · `pause_turn`. Confirmed by inspecting the installed SDK's own signatures and types, not from memory.

**Four things the skill adds or says differently:**

1. **The skill's "`output_format` is deprecated" warning applies to `messages.create()`, not to `messages.parse()`** — whose signature takes `output_format` and merges it into `output_config.format` itself. Record 0006's review item ("no `output_config={"format": …}` dicts alongside `output_format=Model`") is right; worth one sentence in the record so nobody "fixes" it later.
2. **The skill says to enable server-side `fallbacks` by default on `claude-opus-5`.** Record 0006 explicitly declines it ("a refusal here should be seen, not hidden"). I followed the record. **For Kent.**
3. `temperature`/`top_p`/`budget_tokens` are not merely discouraged on Opus 5 — they return a 400.
4. `anthropic` 1.x is built on **`httpx2`**, not `httpx`. I checked `vcr/patch.py`: vcrpy 8.3.0 patches `httpx2` transports, so cassettes will work. Worth knowing if vcrpy is ever pinned back.

**The citations tension, resolved from the skill.** Structured output is incompatible with `citations: {enabled: true}` on **document** blocks (400). Web search is a different mechanism: its results arrive as their own `web_search_tool_result` content blocks *alongside* the structured text block. `WebSearchToolResultBlock.content` is either a `list[WebSearchResultBlock]` (`url`, `title`, `page_age`, `encrypted_content`) or a single `WebSearchToolResultError` — so a failed search reads as nothing found rather than raising. `found_in` reads those blocks and nothing else, which is S1's set exactly. We declare no document blocks anywhere, so the incompatibility never arises.

## Where I deviated, and why

- **`Outcome` gained `calls` and `cache_write_tokens`; `Receipt` gained `cache_write_tokens`.** Cache writes cost *more* than a fresh token and a run pays them on its first call; a paused answer costs two round trips. A ceiling checked against a number smaller than the truth is not a ceiling. (`Receipt.searches` was already there and the coordinator confirmed it.)
- **`Outcome` has both `about` (the claim the call asked about) and `frontier` (what is still open after folding).** The shapes sheet's `frontier` is the second; a refusal also needs the first to be traceable back to its question.
- **The width cap counts arrows leaving a claim, not claims caused** — otherwise a run could propose arrows for ever. This is what `proposals.md` B4's step 4 actually does.
- **The ending-seeking pass runs after the claim cap too** (B6 says to) and may take the map one claim past it. Only the money stops it. Tested.
- **One known gap, stated in a comment where it lives:** an answer that does not fit the shape raises inside the client library, so that call's counters never reach us. The round trip is counted; its tokens are left at nothing, because nothing is what we know. One call in a run of dozens.
- **`no_path`'s `nearest` has two branches.** When something on the map touches the destination it is a real distance (fewest arrows, walked either way). When nothing does — the common case, since a destination arrives with no arrows — "closest" has no meaning, so the verdict names how far the story *did* get and the sentence says which of the two it is. `proposals.md` B7 assumes a nearest always exists; both branches are computed, neither is invented.

def _best_backed_route(
    graph: Graph, start: PropositionId, goal: PropositionId
) -> tuple[PropositionId, ...]:
    """Find the route from one claim to another whose weakest arrow is strongest.

    The widest bottleneck: the road with the highest low bridge, rather than the
    shortest one. How well-backed each arrow is comes from the word our own
    pipeline wrote on it, which is the same table the change list ranks with.

    Feedback arrows — a market changing the world it is measuring — are set aside,
    which is the rule the whole engine reads a map by. Two routes that are equally
    well-backed are separated by taking the shorter one, and then the one whose
    first differing arrow comes earlier in the map's own list.

    Args:
        graph: The map to walk.
        start: The claim to walk from.
        goal: The claim to walk to.

    Returns:
        The route, claim by claim, starting at `start`. Empty when there is none.
    """
    arrows = [
        (position, arrow) for position, arrow in enumerate(graph.links) if not arrow.reflexive
    ]
    widest: dict[PropositionId, float] = {start: 1.0}
    route: dict[PropositionId, tuple[PropositionId, ...]] = {start: (start,)}
    steps: dict[PropositionId, tuple[int, ...]] = {start: ()}

    # One pass can only push a route one arrow further, so as many passes as there
    # are claims is always enough, and the bound also means a map that somehow
    # held a loop could not spin here.
    for _ in range(len(graph.propositions)):
        settled = True
        for position, arrow in arrows:
            if arrow.source not in widest:
                continue
            reaching = min(widest[arrow.source], PROVENANCE_WEIGHT[arrow.provenance])
            walked = (*route[arrow.source], arrow.target)
            taken = (*steps[arrow.source], position)
            if arrow.target in widest:
                so_far = (widest[arrow.target], -len(route[arrow.target]))
                now = (reaching, -len(walked))
                if now < so_far or (now == so_far and taken >= steps[arrow.target]):
                    continue
            widest[arrow.target] = reaching
            route[arrow.target] = walked
            steps[arrow.target] = taken
            settled = False
        if settled:
            break
    return route.get(goal, ())

===== STANDING_TEXT 638 words
You are helping somebody think through what an event they expect would set off,
step by step, until the story reaches something they could actually trade.

You do this one step at a time. Each time we ask, we show you the map as it
stands and point at one claim on it, and you answer with a single next piece.
Somebody watches the map grow as your answers arrive, so a small, well-argued
piece beats a large, vague one.

What a claim is.
A claim is something that will be plainly true or false by a date, settled by a
named source. "Tensions ease" is not a claim, because two honest people will
never agree on whether it happened. "At least fourteen consecutive days of
unrestricted commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz, counted by Lloyd's
List, by the first of November" is a claim, because they will. Every claim you
write carries the test, the name of whoever applies it, and the day by which the
answer is known.

Start from the outside, then come inside. Before you say how likely this claim
is, ask what set of past cases it belongs to, how many of them came out true, and
out of how many. Say what that set was, precisely enough that somebody else could
count it again. Then say how likely this particular claim is, with the honest
range around it — wide when you are reaching, narrow when you are on familiar
ground. The range is how sure you are of your own number. Where there is no
honest set of past cases, leave it out; absent is better than invented.

What an arrow is.
An arrow is a claim about a mechanism: this happening moves the odds of that.
It says which way and how hard it pushes, how many whole days it takes to arrive,
and what it does over time — a spike that fades, a switch that stays on, or a
climb that builds and then holds. It says whether the push survives its cause
going away: a toppled domino stays down, while an apple only stays up while the
desk is under it. And it says, in one to three sentences, why the mechanism is
real. An arrow with a number and no reason is worth nothing to the person reading
it.

Where the backing comes from.
Use the search tool when the ground is checkable and you are not certain of it,
and cite only addresses the search returned to you in this same call. If you did
not search, or nothing useful came back, cite nothing and say what you know in
the reason instead. An empty list of citations is an honest answer we can show.
An address you are recalling rather than reading is not backing, and we will not
treat it as backing.

How a story ends.
A chain ends either at something somebody could put money on — a contract at a
named venue with the side you would take, or an instrument with a direction and
how far you expect its price to move — or at a plain statement that there is
nothing to trade here, and why. Both are good endings. An ending that trails off
into prose is not.

What an answer is.
Exactly one of three things:
  a new claim, together with the one arrow that reaches it from a claim already
  on the map;
  an arrow between two claims that are both already on the map;
  or a note that this part of the story is finished, with one sentence saying
  why.

You never name a new claim with anything but its words. The short names in the
map we show you are ours; point at one when you name a cause, and never invent
another.

Add the one sentence about `messages.parse(output_format=…)` versus the skill's deprecation note as a comment in `client.py`, where someone would otherwise "fix" it.

input.message:
Coordinator to F — your fix is open as pull request #29 and green; thank you. One more small job on the same branch and worktree (`/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/fix-04-observe-direction`, branch `fix/04-observe-direction` — I added two `spec(multiverse):` sweep commits on top of yours and pushed; pull nothing, just work on the tip). You may commit; do not push.

**A pre-existing flaky property test, found by another agent on a rare seed:** `backend/tests/unit/domain/test_propagation.py::test_observe_may_update_ancestors`. The failing draw had a cause whose `prior.p` was about `3.4e-289`: the test's `assume(any(0.0 < prior.p < 1.0))` lets through a number that is zero for every practical purpose, so observing the target moves nothing upstream and the assertion fails. It passed again after the git-ignored Hypothesis example database was cleared, so it will bite continuous integration one day on a bad seed.

Fix it at the root, by the house rule: **property tests build their inputs, never `assume()` most of them away.** Read the test and `backend/tests/strategies.py`. Either draw the priors this test needs from a strategy bounded well away from 0 and 1 (say why the margin is what it is — it should follow from something the engine or the fixture already states, such as a belief's two-significant-figure floor, not from a number you pick), or build the map the test needs constructively. Do not weaken the assertion. Check whether any other test in `tests/unit/domain/` has the same `assume`-on-a-denormal hole and fix those the same way. Owned files for this job: `backend/tests/unit/domain/test_propagation.py`, `backend/tests/strategies.py`, and any sibling test with the same hole. Touch nothing under `src/`.

Prove it: run the test with a high example count (for instance `--hypothesis-seed` over several seeds, or `@settings(max_examples=…)` temporarily raised — and put it back), then the whole suite, ruff, ruff format, and `mypy --strict src/katalyst/domain`. One `test:` commit. Report only: the root cause in two sentences, what you changed, and the verification tails.

M finished the pipeline, and I've reviewed it and sent it back for one fix round. Nothing has been recorded or spent yet.

**What I checked myself:**
- The suite passes (333 tests, with the recording tests set aside), and lints and both type checks are clean.
- M touched no file outside its owned list.
- The price table matches what I read from the `claude-api` skill.
- I read the standing prompt end to end. It is plain and has no numbers or jargon, and I found one problem in it, listed below.

**What I sent back:**
- **`expand.py` is 1,622 lines.** M's own six sections are modules in all but name, so it splits into `outcome`, `grounding`, `expand`, `grow` and `verify`, with no behaviour change.
- **Two path rules where you ruled one.** The Verify door re-implements the best-backed route that `domain/diff.py` already has. Your K5 ruling was one path-choosing rule, used twice.
- **The vendor library leaks.** M says the library is imported only in `client.py`, but `expand.py` imports a vendor type too. M now fixes that and adds a test that enforces it.
- **The prompt's example of a good claim is the Hormuz fixture's own claim.** The Hormuz recording would partly echo an answer we handed the model, so M will pick an example from a domain none of the four hypotheses touches.
- **Past the search cap, keep the search tool declared and forbid its use.** The tool list sits at the front of the cached prompt, so removing the tool would throw the cache away at full price. M found this, and the chapter is updated.

All of this lands before recording because cassettes match on the request body, and any prompt change would invalidate them.

**One thing you should know:** the `claude-api` skill's default for `claude-opus-5` is to turn on server-side fallbacks, which quietly re-run a refused call on another model. Your record 0006 declines that on purpose, so a refusal is shown rather than hidden. M followed the record, and I'm leaving it off unless you say otherwise.

**One pre-existing flaky test:** M hit it on a rare seed. A property test lets a prior of about 1e-289 through its `assume`. F is fixing it at the root on the fix branch, which sits under everything else.

Three agents are running: J (the join), M (fix round) and F (the flaky test). Pull requests #29, #30 and #31 are open.

# Report — agent J, 04a pull request 2: the join

## What I built

**`ApiWorldSource` asks the three routes.** `readWorld` → `POST /api/worlds`, `readDiff` → `POST /api/worlds/diff`, `readConditional` → `POST /api/worlds/conditional`, with the map itself still read once from `/api/fixtures/{id}` and kept (a map is written by hand; a world never is). `App.tsx` hands the canvas an `ApiWorldSource` and falls back to `FixtureWorldSource` when the engine cannot answer, printing the failure's own sentence under the map beside "…the illustrative ones somebody wrote down rather than anything worked out".

**Every slot in the plan's table fills in**, verified against the live engine: model chips (`.36 (.22–.50)` for H, `.40 (.25–.55)` for B…), `WorldView.versions` → record 0014's *computed* sentence, the fifth state `shifted` with `.36 ▼ .081` on the tile, the rail in the engine's own order with **how firm** and **same direction**, the retraction badge off `World.retractions`, the wire's conditional fetched on selection (`H→B` reads `.58 (.42–.73)`).

**The six buttons move numbers.** Each appends an edit; the whole branch goes back for a new world and a new difference. Pressing **Suppose this is true** on B moves M1 `.46 ▲ .52` and M2 `.43 ▲ .54` and writes the engine's summary sentence. **Split this claim** stays visibly not built; **Add a claim** says it needs the part that drafts a claim and records nothing.

**A refused branch shows every reason at once** in a new `Refusal` block in the panel — the map stays readable behind it, drawn structurally with its absences.

**The browser's states became a hint.** `graph/diff/agreement.ts` states the rule tying them to the engine's; `test_the_browser_states_agree_with_the_engine` is un-skipped and pins it; the end-to-end test checks it against the real engine (6 `shifted`, 1 `added`, R `untouched`).

**The Inspector's full decomposition** — what a claim started at, every push on it with its receipt, what the engine came to — laid out, never added up, with that said on screen.

- The arrival wave never settled once the engine's answer arrived inside 1.2 s (the timer lived in an effect the answer re-ran), so the whole map stayed invisible. It now settles on its own clock.
- A claim standing on a supposition was reporting `.40 ▲ >.99` — the stored `1.0` wearing the certainty guard. The movement reading is now suppressed on the tile, in the panel and on the rail (`railRows`), which say the word instead.

## What changed

**The envelope.** `client.py` gains `OneProposal` — a frozen model with a single `proposal: Proposal` field. `_ask` sends that instead of the bare union; `what_it_said` takes it off before building `Said`. It exists for the wire and nothing else: no field of any proposal is renamed, `Proposal` is still the discriminated union of three shapes, and `expand` receives a plain `Proposal` exactly as before. `StartingClaim` is already an object at the top (`type: object`, `$defs` alongside) and is sent unwrapped.

**`wire_schema(shape)`** returns the exact description the library will send — the shape's own JSON schema after the library's tidying pass. It uses one private path into the SDK (`anthropic.lib._parse._transform.transform_schema`), in the one module allowed to know vendor internals, never to build a request, with a comment saying that if it moves the import fails loudly at start-up.

**`test_wire_schema.py`** (14 tests, both shapes) pins what the service demands. **`prompt_hash` now covers the shapes as they go out** rather than as they are written, since the tidied description is what the model is actually asked for: `93f8598…`. Nothing is recorded, so nothing is stale.

**`proposals.md` open question 2** rewritten in my worktree: answered *no*, with the service's sentence quoted, the envelope described as wire-only, and the note that the library and the service disagreed — which is why reading the library was not enough.

## The risks I found by reading

Measured: `OneProposal` is 15.9 KB, 10 named shapes, deepest nesting 9, largest object 10 properties; `StartingClaim` 5.1 KB.

**Clean, and now pinned by tests.** No unsupported keyword survives — the library strips every numeric and string constraint (`minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `minLength`, …), so none reaches the wire. Every one of the 11 objects carries `additionalProperties: false`. The only string format is `date`, which is supported. No recursion. `tuple[X, ...]` is homogeneous so it emits a plain array — no `prefixItems`; a fixed-length tuple would, and the test now forbids one. Every `$ref` resolves. Multi-valued `Literal`s survive as real `enum`s (`mode`, `shape`, `claim_kind`, `side`, `direction`), so those *are* constrained by the service.

**Fixed.** *A discriminator is a hint, not a constraint, and on a payoff it is optional too.* The library moves a single-valued `const` into the description (`{"type":"string", "description":"… {const: claim}"}`) even though the bundle lists `const` as supported — so the model reads `kind` from prose. Worse, `ContractPayoff.kind` and `PricePayoff.kind` carry defaults in `domain/`, so they are **absent from `required`**: a model can legitimately omit the one field that tells the two payoff shapes apart, and pydantic then has nothing to route on. I could not fix the defaults (they are `domain/proposition.py`, not mine), so I spent the risk where it is cheapest and inside my own files: `ClaimProposal.payoff`'s description now names `kind` and both its values. **Worth a look from whoever owns `domain/proposition.py`** — giving those two fields no default would remove the hazard outright.

**Unsettled by the skill, left as they are, with the one-line fix named.**
- *Optional properties are absent from `required`.* The bundle requires only `additionalProperties: false` per object and nowhere says every property must be required; its tool guidance explicitly endorses optional parameters. Our optional fields mean what they say — an absent base rate is absent, not `null`. If the service objects, the fix is to make every field required and `| None`, which changes no meaning because each already accepts null.
- *Nested `anyOf`.* `payoff` is `anyOf[ anyOf[Contract, Price], null ]`. `anyOf` is supported and nothing says it may not nest; if it turns out it may not, flattening to `anyOf[Contract, Price, null]` is the fix.
- *No documented limit* on schema size, property count or nesting depth. Ours are small; the first successful call settles it.

**Already the designed path.** Because numeric constraints never reach the service, a likelihood outside 0–1 or a base rate with `n = 0` comes back as an answer we could not read — a refusal with a plain sentence, and G4's silent retry asks again. That is what `Ranged`'s own validator is for and it is documented there.

| `verify.py` | The Verify door: a graded path or an honest `no_path`. No code path adds an arrow to make a path exist. It uses the **one** best-backed-route rule, now public in `domain/diff.py` |

input.message:
Coordinator to J — the fix round verifies for me (215 tests, 3 end-to-end passed when I ran them) and the collision, the status line and the dock all look right; your correction about the 21-pixel wire lane is accepted. One short last round, all from `light-13-moved-only-by-reweighting.png`:

1. **`.36 ▲ .36   up · no change`** — an arrow between two numbers that print the same, saying "up" and "no change" at once, reads as a bug. One rule: **never draw a chevron between two readings that print identically.** When before and after print the same at two significant figures, print the one reading, and say the move in words with the size of the move itself at two significant figures with the usual guard (here the engine's move is about `.0090`) — for instance `.36 · up by .0090`. Apply it wherever a before/after pair is drawn (tile movement row, rail row, Inspector headline), not only here; add `test_no_chevron_between_two_readings_that_print_the_same`.
2. **The explanation under it is false for this case.** "…a move counts only when the versions of the map agree on which way it went, and these did not" — the versions did not disagree; none that counts moved at all. When the engine's row says `moved_only_by_reweighting`, the FIRST line of WHAT YOUR EDIT DID is the sentence, word for word — *"this claim moved only because the observation made some versions count more."* (W's `inspector.md` puts it first, above the decomposition) — and the "versions did not agree" paragraph and the `same direction 0%` row are not shown for that claim, because a share of nothing is not a disagreement. Keep the general paragraph for the ordinary unchanged case. The sentence must be visible at 1600 × 1000 without scrolling the section; re-shoot it in both themes.
3. **An observed claim shows the stored `1.0`** — C reads `>.99 (>.99–>.99)` on its model chip and `.40 ▲ >.99` on its movement row. The round-2 rule is one rule, not a rule about suppositions only: a claim whose value an edit fixed prints its **word**, read from the world's `states` — *Supposed · date* for a supposition, *Happened · date* for an observation — and no surface but the path product reads the stored `1.0`. You already do this for the supposed strike tile; do the same for an observed claim: chip, movement row, rail and Inspector. Check `spec/workbench/tiles-ports-wires.md` and `diff-view.md` say it for both; if they say it only for a supposition, fix the sentence.

Re-run `npm run check` and `npx playwright test`, re-shoot `13-…` and one picture of the observed claim in both themes, commit, and report only what changed and the verification tails.

The join is one short round from a pull request. I verified J's fix round myself: 215 browser tests and all three end-to-end tests pass, the tile collision is gone, and the status line is true.

J found the cause of the collision. A tile was laid out at its old height while pinned in place. Its fix:
- A tile reserves room for its movement line from the moment a branch opens, so nothing jumps when the numbers arrive.
- Every pin is dropped whenever any tile changes size. J tried dropping pins one at a time first, and a test caught the neighbour problem that causes.

Looking at the reweighting screen (observing C) turned up three more problems. They are back with J as a short last round:
- **A chevron between identical numbers.** H showed `.36 ▲ .36 · up · no change`. The rule is now: never draw a chevron between two readings that print the same. Print the one number and say the move in words, with the size of the move itself.
- **Your G3 sentence was buried.** A paragraph above it claimed the versions "did not agree", which is false for a claim moved only by reweighting. That sentence now comes first, and the wrong paragraph is not shown for that claim.
- **An observed claim printed the stored `1.0` as `>.99`.** It should print its word, *Happened · Oct 1*, the way a supposed claim already prints *Supposed*.

J also proposed a fourth entry for the vocabulary's "words for a number that is not there". It covers a number the engine refused to work out, as distinct from one nobody has worked out yet: **not worked out**, with the reason naming the refusal. I've accepted it in principle. It follows your "a word must mean what it says" ruling.

Running: J (last round) and M (the stream). Open pull requests are #29 (the engine fix), #30 (generation chapters), #31 (canvas chapter) and #32 (the pipeline). Spend is $0.64 of $500. Still waiting on you, and blocking nothing: the tile-height ceiling, 272 in the chapter against 320 in the code.
