<note>This agent stopped with background work of its own still running. It may resume on its own when that work completes or reports, and the same task-id notifies again if it does; the result below may be interim.</note>
<result>The stream is built and green. One thing I stopped on rather than choosing.

## What I built

**`engine/events.py`** — the eight events, with `Verdict` and `Done.reason` imported from where they already live rather than restated. One table, `NAMES`, is the only place the eight are listed; `framed()` writes `event:`/`data:` and a blank line, payload on one line of sorted JSON.

**`api/generate.py`** — the three routes. `POST /api/generate` is a plain `StreamingResponse`; the same route serves a live run and a replay, with no fallback between them. It stops calling the model when the client goes away **by abandoning the walk's own generator** — no flag anyone has to remember to check — and closes it in a `finally`.

**`engine/transcript.py`** — the working, in memory, bounded, dropped oldest-first, with the map held under the same key so it can never outlive the transcript that explains it. Each line carries **the seconds and the thinking tokens**, which are on no event.

**`engine/replay.py`** — the file format, the exact-after-trimming match, and playback. The receipt is rebuilt to zeros; the likelihoods are recomputed from the header's seed, so a recording holds no world. `faults_in()` is what the build reads.

**`api/health.py`** — `replayable`, and `status` is `ready` when there is a key *or* something to replay.

**Loop-size ceilings, measured** (this machine, 2026-09-17, written beside the constants): Hormuz takes **394 ms** at 8 000 × 16 = 128 000 worlds; scaled to a 30-claim map by `propagation.md`'s measured claim-linearity that is ~1.7 s, and the worst request — a comparison, two worlds, on a build machine ~2.5× slower — is **~8.4 s**. `MOST_VERSIONS = 8_000`, `MOST_WORLDS = 16`, against a stated ten-second budget. Refused with 422, never clamped.

**nginx** gets `proxy_buffering off`, `proxy_cache off`, `chunked_transfer_encoding on` and long read/send timeouts; every answer also carries `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. **`recordings` CI job** passes on an empty folder. **`make record-demo ONLY=… CAP=…`**, `CAP` only ever lowering the figure in code. Scrubbing moved into `tests/conftest.py`.

**Your three items.** (1) `HOW_HARD_TO_TRY` is a pinned module constant — **left as `None`, so nothing is sent**, because adding `output_config.effort` changes the request body and the cassettes match on it; the constant, its reasoning and the re-record cost are documented there. (2) Seconds and thinking tokens now flow `Said → Outcome → TranscriptLine`; `prompt_hash` is unchanged (`93f8598…`) and all eight cassettes still replay. (3) Left alone.

## The one thing I stopped on

**There is no question shape for drafting a claim somebody named.** `replay.md` B4 requires every recording's header to carry one scripted intervention, "drafted live when the recording was made". `ClaimProposal` carries exactly one arrow and it points *into* the new claim — but "…but Iran is struck the next day" causes things, so its arrows point *out*. No chapter defines a third answer shape, and I must not touch the prompt or the proposal shapes in this pull request.

So: the **replay half** of `POST /api/generate/insert` is built and tested (scripted sentence matched exactly, recorded `Insert` handed back, validated against the map with the same `validate` and the same codes, anything else declined with *"drafting a new claim needs a model key."*). The **live half** is not. `make record-demo` runs the whole generation, checks it showed a refusal, and then stops with a plain sentence naming the gap and the two ways on — add the shape and its prompt in the batched prompt round, or `--without-the-scripted-insert` to record now and add it later. I did not pick.

**So `make record-demo ONLY=hormuz CAP=15` will stop before writing unless you pass `--without-the-scripted-insert`.** Your call.

## For decision record 0009

It is not mine to edit. Line 44 currently reads *"One workflow, four jobs… (Amended 2026-09-17: five — stack 03b added `e2e`…)"*. The sentence it needs:

> *(Amended 2026-09-17: six — stack 04b added `recordings`, which reads every committed recording and needs no key. Still no key in any of them.)*

And line 58's required-checks list needs `recordings` added, or the job runs without being required.

## Outside my stated grant — all chapter-mandated, none chosen by me

`engine/worlds.py` (the chapter puts `MOST_VERSIONS`/`MOST_WORLDS` there, and `streaming.md` requires the lookup to answer from stored examples *then* this process's generations — one new public `example_named`, three call sites); `settings.py` (`replay.md`: `instant` "is a setting, read by `katalyst.settings`"); `engine/grow.py` (annotation only, `Iterator` → `Generator`, so the route can close it); `tests/api/test_health.py` (follows `Readiness`); `engine/record.py` and `engine/check_recordings.py` (new engine modules).

## Verification

```
407 passed, 1 warning in 73.37s        # whole suite, no key, zero failures
TOTAL   1165   0   288   0   100%      # domain/ coverage
ruff check .            → All checks passed!
ruff format --check .   → 82 files already formatted
mypy --strict src/katalyst/domain → Success: no issues found in 12 source files
mypy src                → Success: no issues found in 43 source files
check_recordings        → "No recordings … Nothing to check, and nothing wrong with that."
```

**`docker compose build` I could not run**: it stalls resolving `docker.io/docker/dockerfile:1` and a bare `docker pull` returns nothing, so this environment has no registry access. The nginx change is covered by a test that reads the `/api/` location for `proxy_buffering off` and `proxy_cache off`, plus a timing test on the route itself; the `docker` job will build it.

## The stream, on 8042, with no key

```
GET /api/readyz
{"status":"ready","model_key_present":false,
 "replayable":[{"example":"hormuz","recording_date":"2026-09-17"}]}

content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8   cache-control: no-store   x-accel-buffering: no

event: generation_started
data: {"generation_id":"a-recorded-run","hypothesis":"The Strait of Hormuz is going to open next week.","seed":20261001,"target":null}

event: proposal_accepted
data: {"at":0,"frontier":["H"],"links":[],"proposition":{…}}
…
event: receipt
data: {"calls":0,"dollars":0.0,"mode":"replay","model":"claude-opus-5",…}

event: done
data: {"claims":3,"links":2,"reason":"reached_terminal","rejected":1}
```

Timed as they arrived: `81.75 generation_started · 82.38 · 82.93 · 83.57 proposal_rejected · 84.18 · 84.77 beliefs_propagated · 85.40 receipt · 85.99 done` — **4.2 seconds between the first and the last**, nothing buffered.

One commit, `2d77594`, on `feat/04b-stream`. Stopping here.</result>

content.text:
The first full Hormuz run finished without a crash, but the recorder kept nothing from it. I've sent that back to M to fix before I run again.

**What happened**
- Sixteen proposals were accepted and none was refused. The run took 9 minutes 7 seconds, about one new tile every half minute, arriving in bursts.
- The recorder then refused to write a recording, because record 0012 says every recording must show at least one refusal. That is the right call under the rule as it stands.
- The recorder also discarded the receipt, the per-call timings and the finished map. I can't tell you the true cost of a run you paid for.
- I've booked it at an upper estimate of $3, so the running total is about **$3.64 of $500**.
- M is making a paid run impossible to discard. The recorder will always print the receipt, and it will always keep the full transcript in a git-ignored folder outside `recordings/`. M is also adding a measure-only mode. After that I'll run again and report real numbers.

**A question for you, which I'll put to you with the rest of the batch.** Your rule that "every recording shows a refusal" assumes the model errs. On this run it never did, which says the prompt is doing its job. I see three options:
- **Re-run until a refusal appears.** This costs money each time and may never produce one.
- **Relax the rule.** A recording shows every refusal that happened, and says plainly when there were none.
- **Grow larger maps.** Loops and bad proposals arise naturally in bigger maps.

I'll bring this to you with the measured run, together with the other batched items: unsourced base rates, the missing shape for a claim the user names, the market/event classification wobble, and thinking effort against pace.

G (the growing canvas) and M (the recorder fix) are still running.

Open pull requests are #29–#33. Still waiting on you, and blocking nothing: the tile-height ceiling, which is 272 in the chapter and 320 in the code.

Coordinator to F — your flaky-test fix is pushed and #29 is green. One more defect in your file, found by a property test on a rare draw on another branch. Same worktree and branch (`/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/fix-04-observe-direction`, `fix/04-observe-direction`); commit, do not push.

**`domain/diff.py::_two_figures` leaks scientific notation.** `f"{likelihood:#.2g}"` switches to exponent form below 1e-4, and the guard only catches a value that is exactly nothing, so `test_summary_matches_the_template` failed with: *"…moves The Strait of Hormuz reopens… from >.99 to 1.0e-09 by 2026-01-01…"* (a generated map whose priors are all 0.0, with a supposition on a market claim). A sentence on screen must never read `1.0e-09`.

Fix it as a defect, with no change of policy: the browser's `toTwoFigures` (`frontend/src/components/BeliefChip.tsx` on branch `feat/04a-join`, readable at `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04a-join/frontend/src/components/BeliefChip.tsx`) already writes the same rule with no exponent form — two significant figures as a plain decimal however small, `<.01` only at nothing or below, `>.99` at one or when rounding carries to one. Make the engine's function say exactly what the browser's says for every input, including the carry case (`.995`, `.0999`). Where the guard should *begin* (whether a likelihood under .01 should print `<.01`) is a question going to Kent — do not decide it; say in the docstring that the two implementations are one rule written twice and must move together, and name the browser function.

Tests, none with a typed-in engine number: a property test over floats in [0, 1] that the written form never contains `e`, always matches the template's own pattern, and reads back within two significant figures of the input; a table test of the edge cases above. Check whether any other place in `domain/` or `engine/worlds.py` formats a likelihood by hand and route it through this one function. Owned files: `backend/src/katalyst/domain/diff.py` (`_two_figures` and its callers only), its tests. Run the suite, lints and strict typing; one `fix(diff):` commit; report what changed and the tails.

**Where things stand:** the second full Hormuz run is going. It is capped at $15 in code, and the recorder now keeps every paid run whatever happens. Three jobs are in flight, and five pull requests (#29–#33) are open for you.

**Since the last update:**
- **M's recorder fix is verified.** Every paid run is now kept under a git-ignored `backend/.runs/` folder. It holds the receipt, the per-call seconds and thinking tokens, the finished map, and the events. `make run-demo` does a measurement run without writing a recording.
- **M also found two bugs that would have ruined the first real recording.** One was a header pointing at a map that nothing could find. The other collected the growth events and then threw them away.
- **My own test run hit a rare engine defect that M's run did not.** On an unusual generated map, the summary sentence printed a likelihood as `1.0e-09`. The browser prints the same value as `.0000000010`. One rule is written in two places, and they disagree. F is making the engine match the browser, on #29, without changing any policy.

**Running now:**
- The Hormuz run. When it finishes I report the true cost, the time, where the time goes, and what a whole generated map looks like.
- G, building the growing canvas against the stream.
- F, the formatting defect.

**The batch of decisions I'll bring you after the run.** All of these change the prompt or a rule you set. Each prompt change means re-recording, so they go together with the measured run in front of you:
1. Base rates arrive as precise counts with no source, for example "305 of 312".
2. "Every recording shows a refusal" was never satisfied, because on the first run the model was never refused.
3. "Add a claim" has no proposal shape for a claim the user names.
4. The model classified the same claim as both `market` and `event`, and two schema descriptions still echo Hormuz.
5. Thinking effort against the pace of about a minute per call.
6. Where `<.01` should begin, which touches K2.
7. The tile-height ceiling: the chapter says 272 and the code says 320.

Spend so far is an upper estimate of about $3.64 of $500.

**The first screen:** four cards that run live, run from a recording (badge + day), or say *not yet live*; record 0012's sentence word for word with the day from `/api/readyz`; the input bar with three fields, one **Build the map** button and an explicit *I don't know*.

**Hand-me-downs.** (1) The fourth absence kind `refused` with its row in `spec/vocabulary.md` and a paragraph on why it is not a shade of `no_engine`. (2) The canvas library's credit: its licence is MIT and asks only that the notice travel with the software; the library itself asks that the credit be hidden only by paying subscribers. We pay for nothing and hide nothing — the canvas now reserves a 24 px row at its foot and the credit drops into it, so it can never land on a tile. (3) The six missing tests written in `tile.test.tsx` (the six-regions one says in so many words that a skeleton is a box, not a tile) and **seven** `focusMap` tests renamed from sentences to the names their chapter gives — I renamed all seven rather than guessing which four, and `colourLaw`'s reduced-motion test moved to `motionBudget.test.ts`, which INV-workbench.73 names and which did not exist. (4) The tile-height ceiling untouched; I deliberately did **not** write `test_tile_height_is_content_fit_within_152_and_272`. (5) `pathProduct` left as the join's honest absence. (6) **Add a claim** built and exercised both ways against the real route.

- **`Growth` has three fields the chapter's block does not list** — `seed`, `hypothesis`, `target` — all read off `generation_started`. The map's title, the origin sentence and the verdict card's destination need them.

And the keyboard follows the growing edge (the newest claim takes focus, the existing rule for a newly created claim), so a nine-minute run does not build off-screen; nothing re-frames and nothing re-lays out.
- **No token added.** `tokens.css` untouched.

## Chapter numbers my change made stale

None that I can see. Everything I built is `streaming-growth.md` as written. Two things the chapter should eventually record: it says the receipt strip and the Inspector's copy both print the nine fields — on a 1000 px screen that is the same nine numbers twice in one panel, and it is worth a sentence saying that is deliberate. And open question 5 (how long a refusal strip may get) now has an answer in the code: the panel scrolls as a whole rather than section by section, and `generationDock.css` says why.

## Open questions / things for you

1. **Server bug, replay path, not mine to fix.** `GET /api/generate/{generation_id}/transcript` 404s for every replayed run: `api/generate.py::_replayed` remembers the transcript under `recording.header.base_id` (the map's id) while `generation_started.generation_id` carries the *recorded* run's name. Confirmed by curl: `/api/generate/a-recorded-run/transcript` → "no longer holding that generation"; `/api/generate/01AAAA…/transcript` → the transcript. The browser asks by the name the stream gave and prints the route's own sentence, which is the honest behaviour — but the working is unreadable on a replay until the server keys it by `generation_id`.
2. **No setting for the recordings folder**, as you suspected. `engine/replay.RECORDINGS` is a module constant (`Path(__file__).parents[3] / "recordings"`); `summaries()` and `find()` take a `folder` argument that `api/health.py` and `api/generate.py` never pass. 4. **The card-to-recording match** relies on the launchpad's `example` key equalling `RecordingSummary.example` (the recording's file stem). `hormuz` matches; the other three are my guesses (`midterms`, `export-controls`, `photonics`). 5. **NFR-7's wording** still reads "within 1s of the first token". The chapter corrects it; the requirement itself is not mine to edit. The sentence it should carry: *streaming first paint within 1 s of the request being accepted — a reserved rectangle at its column.*

I now have what I need to bring you the batch of questions. First, the facts.

**The measured run (Hormuz, live, default settings).**
- 10 calls, 9 searches, **$1.32**.
- **10 min 54 s**, and 61% of everything the model wrote was thinking.
- It built 10 claims and 9 arrows. None were refused. It stopped at the width cap.
- The map is good. Hormuz leads to Brent, to VLCC rates (short Frontline), and to Qatari LNG. LNG leads to TTF, JKM and EU storage at 80%. Storage leads to Q1-2027 TTF, German power and a calendar spread.
- Every ending names a real instrument and a real judge: ICE, CME, Baltic Exchange, AGSI+.
- 8 of the 9 arrows are `documented`, with sources the search actually returned.
- The pace is about one tile a minute, and it is sequential by nature. Each call has to see the map as it stands, so "three at once" only helps when three different claims are open.

**What I'm fixing without asking.** Each of these is a defect or follows from something you already decided.

## What I built

**The stream, read and folded.** `frontend/src/stream/` is new: `events.ts` hand-types the eight events exactly as the chapter gives them (plus the one readiness field `schema.ts` does not carry yet, in `readiness.ts`); `generate.ts` is one async generator over `POST /api/generate` read as a stream — no `EventSource`, no component touching the network, no invented seed, and **"I don't know" sends no `user_belief` at all**; `growth.ts` is the pure reducer; `transcript.ts` and `insert.ts` read the other two routes.

**The map draws itself.** A reserved rectangle (`SkeletonTile`, 280 × 152, dashed hairline on `--surface`, one line, no digit, not selectable, not focusable, no animation but opacity) stands at the growing edge; the rectangles are the frontier, rebuilt from *either* growth event and emptied on `beliefs_propagated`. Claims and their arrows arrive one at a time through the existing canvas — `toFlow` gained a third node kind and a layout-only arrow that pulls a rectangle into the column after the claim it hangs off, so nothing already placed moves. `beliefs_propagated` replaces the world wholesale through **the one** `toWorldView` that `ApiWorldSource` already called (I widened its second argument from a `FixtureBundle` to a four-field `WorldSummary`).

**The dock:** the Verify door's two cards, the refusal strip (one row per refusal, one line per rule broken, the rule's own sentence, its code never drawn), the receipt strip (nine labelled fields, nothing added up), **Add a claim**, the line saying why the run stopped, and the Inspector — which gained the chapter's third subject, `{kind: "generation"}`, with the receipt and the whole working.

**The first screen:** four cards that run live, run from a recording (badge + day), or say *not yet live*; record 0012's sentence word for word with the day from `/api/readyz`; the input bar with three fields, one **Build the map** button and an explicit *I don't know*.

**Hand-me-downs.** (1) The fourth absence kind `refused` with its row in `spec/vocabulary.md` and a paragraph on why it is not a shade of `no_engine`. (2) The canvas library's credit: its licence is MIT and asks only that the notice travel with the software; the library itself asks that the credit be hidden only by paying subscribers. We pay for nothing and hide nothing — the canvas now reserves a 24 px row at its foot and the credit drops into it, so it can never land on a tile. (3) The six missing tests written in `tile.test.tsx` (the six-regions one says in so many words that a skeleton is a box, not a tile) and **seven** `focusMap` tests renamed from sentences to the names their chapter gives — I renamed all seven rather than guessing which four, and `colourLaw`'s reduced-motion test moved to `motionBudget.test.ts`, which INV-workbench.73 names and which did not exist. (4) The tile-height ceiling untouched; I deliberately did **not** write `test_tile_height_is_content_fit_within_152_and_272`. (5) `pathProduct` left as the join's honest absence. (6) **Add a claim** built and exercised both ways against the real route.

## Where I deviated, and why

- **`Growth` has three fields the chapter's block does not list** — `seed`, `hypothesis`, `target` — all read off `generation_started`. The map's title, the origin sentence and the verdict card's destination need them.
- **`Selection` gained a third variant** rather than the Inspector taking a separate subject prop. Additive; nothing else changed.
- **Files outside my list that I touched, minimally.** `PathBar.tsx`: the path-product wart extracted to one exported constant so the card and the bar print one wording (the chapter requires it). `App.test.tsx`: two assertions, because the launchpad's copy changed. `graph/toFlow.ts`, `graph/Canvas.tsx`, `graph/canvas.css`: the third node kind, the badge slot, the credit row, and one guard so the hover lens never dims a reserved rectangle.
- **I did not touch `styles/app.css`.** The first screen needed to be wider than its 660 px column, so `launchpad.css` defines `.column--launchpad` and `App.tsx` uses it. I also did not touch `BranchPanel.tsx`, so the six-button panel on a *stored* map still says **Add a claim** is not connected; the control is live on a generated map only.
- **Two small product calls.** A launchpad card's action reads *Watch it build*, not *Build the map* — the vocabulary says that button is the one on the input bar, and a word naming two controls names neither. And the keyboard follows the growing edge (the newest claim takes focus, the existing rule for a newly created claim), so a nine-minute run does not build off-screen; nothing re-frames and nothing re-lays out.
- **No token added.** `tokens.css` untouched.

## Chapter numbers my change made stale

None that I can see. Everything I built is `streaming-growth.md` as written. Two things the chapter should eventually record: it says the receipt strip and the Inspector's copy both print the nine fields — on a 1000 px screen that is the same nine numbers twice in one panel, and it is worth a sentence saying that is deliberate. And open question 5 (how long a refusal strip may get) now has an answer in the code: the panel scrolls as a whole rather than section by section, and `generationDock.css` says why.

## Open questions / things for you

1. **Server bug, replay path, not mine to fix.** `GET /api/generate/{generation_id}/transcript` 404s for every replayed run: `api/generate.py::_replayed` remembers the transcript under `recording.header.base_id` (the map's id) while `generation_started.generation_id` carries the *recorded* run's name. Confirmed by curl: `/api/generate/a-recorded-run/transcript` → "no longer holding that generation"; `/api/generate/01AAAA…/transcript` → the transcript. The browser asks by the name the stream gave and prints the route's own sentence, which is the honest behaviour — but the working is unreadable on a replay until the server keys it by `generation_id`.
2. **No setting for the recordings folder**, as you suspected. `engine/replay.RECORDINGS` is a module constant (`Path(__file__).parents[3] / "recordings"`); `summaries()` and `find()` take a `folder` argument that `api/health.py` and `api/generate.py` never pass. To develop against a real replay I copied the 04b backend into my scratch directory (their worktree untouched, no git command run there), ran their own `tests/unit/engine/a_recording.written_to()` to write `recordings/hormuz.jsonl` into the copy, and served that on 8043. A setting would make this unnecessary.
3. **`POST /api/generate/insert` resolves `base_id` against stored examples.** It works from a generated map only because the reducer passes `World.base_id` (the map's own id), which the transcript store happens to hold. `base_id = generation_id` is refused with "There is no stored example called …". Worth confirming that is the intended contract.
4. **The card-to-recording match** relies on the launchpad's `example` key equalling `RecordingSummary.example` (the recording's file stem). `hormuz` matches; the other three are my guesses (`midterms`, `export-controls`, `photonics`). A mismatch degrades honestly to *not yet live*, but the recorder should use those names.
5. **NFR-7's wording** still reads "within 1s of the first token". The chapter corrects it; the requirement itself is not mine to edit. The sentence it should carry: *streaming first paint within 1 s of the request being accepted — a reserved rectangle at its column.*

## What I could and could not exercise

- **Could:** the whole replayed run end to end (8 events, one refusal, world, receipt, done); the insert route both ways — an unscripted sentence returns 501 with `drafting a new claim needs a model key.` and the control prints that word for word, and the recording's scripted `…but Iran is struck the next day` returns a checked `Insert`; the transcript rendering (by addressing around bug 1 in a throwaway route, so the rendering itself could be photographed).
- **Could not:** a live run of any kind (no key, by design); the `no_path` and graded-path verdicts against a real server — no recording carries a `verdict`, so those two are driven from hand-written events in the component tests and from a spliced event in the screenshot harness; the branch panel's **Add a claim** (file not mine).

## Visual review checklist, on my own 32 pictures (both themes, 1600 × 1000)

1. **Nothing looks like a component library's default** — pass, after one fix: the three likelihood handles were native range sliders (rounded pill, round grip). They are now a hairline track with a 12 px square grip in the text colour.
2. **No spinner, no pop-up, no dialog to dismiss** — pass. Waiting is a reserved rectangle or an absence with its reason; `test_there_is_no_spinner_anywhere` walks every stylesheet and component.
3. **Greyscale still reads** — pass. Converted `dark-07` and `light-06`: tile silhouettes, the rectangle's dashed border, the three-dot origin mark and the push plate all survive.
4. **No number over two significant figures, none missing its range** — pass. `.40 (.20–.60)`, `.45 (.24–.65)`, path likelihood `.083`. Token counts, calls, cost and duration are counts and measurements, printed whole in the number face with no range.
5. **Every number's origin nameable; no empty slot filled in** — pass. Every chip reads *no engine yet* with its reason while the map grows; the receipt's nine fields open the working in one click.
6. **Layered left to right, no hairball** — pass.
7. **No text under 11 px, nothing under 4.5:1** — pass. The credit is at `--text-sm` (13 px) in its own row. One note: the reserved rectangle's dashed border is `--hairline` (10 %) and faint; the meaning is carried by the words HELD OPEN, not the border.
8. **Tile 280 wide, on the 8 px grid** — pass, measured by `test_tile_is_280_wide_and_on_the_eight_pixel_grid` off the tile's own box and `tileHeight`.
9. **Keyboard only, focus always visible, arrows follow the wires** — pass: the launchpad card is reached and opened with Tab and Enter in `generate.spec.ts`; the map's keys are unchanged.
10. **Reduced motion: ordering there, tweening gone** — pass. `dark-12`/`light-12` are the same mid-growth picture in the same order; `test_reduced_motion_zeroes_every_tween_and_keeps_the_stagger` pins the tokens.
11. **Six buttons and badges word for word** — pass; **Build the map** appears once, on the input bar.
12. **A supposed-then-overridden claim says so** — not reachable on a generated map in this pull request; unchanged on the stored map, where `hormuz.spec.ts` still checks it.
13. **The map grew rather than appeared** — pass, and this is the line this pull request exists for: `05` is a rectangle before any claim, `06` is two claims with a rectangle at the edge and a refusal on screen in the rule's own words, `07` is the finished map with the receipt.

Three answers are in: recordings show what actually happened, anything below .01 prints `<.01`, and the tile ceiling stays at 320 with the chapter corrected. Here is the base rate explained plainly.

**What a base rate is for.** Take a claim on the map: *"Europe ends the injection season with gas storage at least 80% full."* The model gives two things about it.

- **The likelihood**, `.30 (.12–.52)`. This is its judgment about this particular situation.
- **The base rate**, "12 of 15". It answers a different question: in past situations like this one, how often did it come out true? Here the claim is that in 15 past gas-supply scares, storage still reached 80% in 12 of them.

It exists because forecasters do better when they start from how often this kind of thing usually happens and only then adjust for the case in front of them. Your PRD asks for this: every number should be one click from "how often such things have happened before". On screen the base rate sits in the Inspector next to the likelihood, so a reader can see whether `.30` is a bold call against a usual 80% or just the ordinary rate.

**The problem.** The model gets one web search per step, and it always spends it on why the arrow is real (the mechanism). So "12 of 15" was never looked up. It is the model's memory, stated with the precision of a count. Nobody can click through and check which 15 episodes it means.

A reader cannot tell a counted number from a remembered one. That is the "number nobody computed" state you veto.

**The three choices.**

1. **Let it look the count up, and show only what it found.** The model gets a second search, reserved for the reference class. A base rate appears only when it cites a page that search returned. Otherwise the slot says honestly that there is none. This is the same rule you already chose for an arrow's sources.
   - Cost is about a cent per step, plus an estimated 15–30 seconds (I would measure it).
   - Most honest, keeps the feature alive, and slows a live run down.
2. **Same honesty rule, no extra search.** A base rate appears only if it is sourced, and with one search it almost never will be.
   - On this run all 8 would have disappeared.
   - Fast and simple, but the "how often before?" slot would nearly always be empty.
3. **Keep showing them, with a label.** "12 of 15" stays on screen with the words *recalled by the model — not counted from a source*.
   - Nothing slows down and nothing is lost.
   - A precise-looking count that nobody can check still sits next to your real numbers.

I recommend option 1. It treats a base rate exactly as you already treat an arrow's evidence, so there is one rule rather than two.

input.message:
Coordinator to M — the recorder fix verified, and the second run was kept in full: `claude-opus-5`, 10 calls, 9 searches, **$1.32, 10 m 54 s, 61% thinking**, 10 claims, 9 arrows (8 documented), 0 refused, `width_cap`. It is at `backend/.runs/hormuz-2026-09-17T15-20-12Z.json` in your worktree — read it; it is a rich map and it shows every defect below. Kent has now decided the batch: read "Round two" (G7–G11) at the end of `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/notes/2026-09-17-kent-decisions-stack-04.md`. **This is the ONE prompt round** — everything that changes what we send the model lands together, on `feat/04b-stream` (you may now edit the pipeline's files: `engine/{prompt,proposal,client,grounding,expand,grow,outcome,pricing,receipt}.py` and their tests), and I re-record every cassette once at the end. You still hold no key.

**Kent's decisions to build:**
1. **G8 — prototype on Sonnet 5.** The model becomes ONE named setting (default `claude-sonnet-5`, settable to `claude-opus-5`), read once through settings and documented in `.env.example`; `engine/pricing.py` becomes a per-model table (read the prices from the `claude-api` skill, date them); nothing outside `client.py`/`pricing.py`/settings knows which model it is; the receipt already names the model. Verify against the skill for Sonnet 5: `messages.parse` structured output, adaptive thinking, `web_search_20260209`, `tool_choice` none, `pause_turn`, and **the minimum cacheable prefix** (it is model-dependent — make sure the standing text still clears it, and have the zero-cache-reads test say which model it ran on). The prompt hash must not change with the model; the recording header and receipt carry the model.
2. **G7 — base rates are researched.** Per claim call: up to **25 web searches over up to 5 rounds** (a round = one request; you already resume `pause_turn` — cap the resumptions at five and say what happens at the cap: answer with what you have). The prompt tells the model to research the reference class FIRST, to stop as soon as it has a countable class with a source, and that a count it cannot source should be left out. **Our code shows a base rate only when at least one of its sources is a page the search tool returned in that call** (the S1 rule, one function, used for arrows and base rates alike); otherwise the base rate is dropped, the claim is otherwise accepted, and the transcript notes it. The per-generation searches cap rises to fit (an argument; say the default and why); the $15 per-run stop is the safety net — make sure it is checked between rounds, not only between calls. `BaseRate.sources` are plain strings in `domain/` — keep that; match them against returned addresses with `_same_address`.
3. **G9 — no forced refusal.** The recorder and `check_recordings` no longer demand a `proposal_rejected`; a recording with none is valid. Rename/replace `test_every_recording_shows_a_miss` with a test of the new rule (every refusal that occurred is in the file, in order). Remove `--without-the-scripted-insert` once item 6 exists.

**Defects and prompt findings, mine to call, all in this round:**
4. **The hypothesis's resolution came back as junk** — criteria `"Res "`, judge `"x "`, in 7 seconds with 84 thinking tokens, and it was accepted. Find out why from the kept run (is the starting question under-specified? is a schema description misleading? is a constraint missing?). Fix the starting question so the hypothesis gets a real test, a named judge and a date — it may search. Do NOT add a length heuristic to `domain/validity.py`; if you believe INV-1's check needs to be stronger than "not blank", say what rule you would propose and why, and leave `domain/` alone.

input.message:
Coordinator to G — a lot of this is right: the launchpad is dense and honest, the Verify card reads well, the credit row is the correct answer to the licence, and "I don't know" sending nothing is exactly the rule. A fix round from looking at your pictures. Your three server findings were confirmed and are with the server agent (transcript keyed by `generation_id`; a setting for the recordings folder; the insert route's `base_id` contract; example names `hormuz`, `midterms`, `export-controls`, `photonics`).

**A real run to build against.** The coordinator's measured live run is kept in full, with its events, at `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-stream/backend/.runs/hormuz-2026-09-17T15-20-12Z.json` (read-only): **10 claims, 9 arrows, a tree four columns deep, real identifiers (26-character ULIDs, not `H`/`C`/`M1`), long claim sentences, zero refusals, `done.reason = "width_cap"`.** In your scratch copy of the server (never in a worktree, never committed) assemble a recording from its `events` so you can watch a REAL map grow, and drive your component tests' second fixture from the same events. Everything below must hold on that map, not only on the three-claim one.

1. **BLOCKING — tiles land on top of each other as the map grows.** `dark-07-the-finished-map.png` says "three claims, two arrows" and shows two tiles: the market claim sits exactly where the war-risk claim stood in `dark-06` (905, 590 → 905, 575), hiding it, and a wire plate is clipped by the canvas's bottom edge. The join's rule is one rule — a tile is laid out at the height it will be drawn at; a claim ARRIVING keeps every pin; when any box changes size every pin goes — and a reserved rectangle turning into a tile, or a rectangle going away, must obey it too. Find the root cause (my guess: the rectangle's layout-only arrow and its pin outlive the rectangle, or the new tile inherits the rectangle's slot while its sibling keeps the same slot). Extend `test_no_two_tiles_in_a_column_collide` to run after EVERY event of both fixtures (the chapter's worked run and the real 10-claim run), rectangles included: no two boxes of any kind overlap or touch, at every step.
2. **The growing edge must stay where the reader can see it.** On a four-column map at 1600 × 1000 the newest column is under the dock or off the canvas. "Nothing jumps" forbids moving placed tiles; it does not forbid the viewport following. Decide by the chapters (`layout-and-zoom.md` already has a rule for following focus and for creating a claim) and make the growing edge visible without a lurch: say which rule you used. Show me pictures of the real map at steps 3, 6 and 10.
3. **Real identifiers.** The Verify card prints `H → C → M1`. On a generated map those are ULIDs. Never print an identifier on screen: number the steps or use the claim's first words; check every place a stored-map monogram or id was assumed (tile monograms, the rail, the path bar, the transcript, the refusal strip, the status line).
4. **The REPLAY box floats over the canvas** as a paragraph and will cover tiles on a real map. `streaming-growth.md` calls it a badge: make it a compact badge beside the title (word + the recording's day), with the sentence in the dock or the origin strip. Nothing may sit over the map.
5. **The foot of the screen says the same sentence twice** ("The last line closed properly: …" in the status line and again in the `finished` line) across three stacked strips of prose. One place for why the run stopped; the live region announces it once; keep the origin line. Under `width_cap` (the real run) check the sentence reads as a plain fact and blames nobody.
6. **The launchpad's sentence is false when only some examples are recorded**: "these four run from recordings made on 2026-09-17" above three cards reading *not yet live*. Record 0012's sentence is printed word for word only when it is TRUE (all four replayable, one date); otherwise say what is true in the same voice (how many, which day or days). ## G10 — where the guard begins

Split by meaning, in `BeliefChip.tsx`. One shared two-figure core (it keeps the `.995` half-up trick, which is the case the guard exists for), and two functions over it:

- **`toTwoFigures`** — a likelihood, and an end of the range around one, because a range end is a likelihood. The guard is read off the number **as it would print**: two figures at `1.0` or above → `>.99`; below `.010` → `<.01`. So `.0099` → `<.01`, `.010` → `.010`, and `.00996` rounds up onto the line and stays `.010`.
- **`toSize`** — how far a number moved, or how wide a band is. Two figures, no guard, either end: `.0090`, `.0035`, `.00012`, and a move of exactly one prints `1.0`.

Every caller now picks the one that matches. **One was picking wrong, and it was not the move:** the rail's **how firm** column is a band's *width* — a distance between two likelihoods, not a likelihood — and was going through the likelihood formatter. Nothing on the stored example changes (every width there is above a hundredth), but a remarkably firm claim would have read `<.01` where the reader wanted `.0040`. It takes `toSize` now.

The docstring says the rule is written twice and names `backend/src/katalyst/domain/diff.py::_two_figures` as the other copy, with the sentence that they must move together.

Stack 04: not started

- Evals and the scorecard.

content.text:
These are the five pieces of stack 04 that haven't been started. Here is what each one is, why it's there, and what it costs.

## 1. Evals and the scorecard

**What it is.** A command, `make eval`, that runs the four example hypotheses from the assignment through the real model and grades the resulting maps. It checks only structure and never wording:
- Are there any loops?
- Does every map end in something you could trade, or in a plain "nothing to trade here"?
- Does every arrow give a reason?
- Does every `documented` arrow have a source?
- Does every claim say how it will be checked?
- Does the Verify door return a graded path or an honest "no path"?
- One of the four cases is deliberately unreachable, to prove the engine never invents a bridge.

The output is a **scorecard**, a table with one row per example. It shows claims, endings, refusals, base rates kept and dropped, searches, thinking tokens, seconds per call and dollars.

**Why it exists.** Today, when I change the prompt, the only way to know whether it helped is to read a map and form an opinion. The scorecard turns "did that prompt change help?" into a comparison of two rows. It is also the baseline that your earlier decisions point at. The ensemble (record 0015) and the critique pass (FR-9) are both deferred until there is a scorecard to measure them against.

**Cost.** It calls the model, so only I run it, under the $15 stop. It is not part of the build, because continuous integration never gets a key.

## 2. The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths

**What it is.** The engine computes every likelihood 2,000 times, on 2,000 slightly different versions of the map, to get a range like `.35 (.22–.50)`. Today only each claim's starting number varies between versions. Every arrow's strength is treated as exactly known.

This piece makes arrow strengths vary too. How much each one varies is derived from how well-backed the arrow is:

| The arrow is… | Its strength wobbles… |
|---|---|
| `documented` (cites a source) | a little (0.15) |
| `argued` (a rationale, no source) | more (0.40) |
| `asserted` (neither) | a lot (0.60) |

You settled this in record 0014. "How well-backed is this arrow?" becomes "how wide is the range downstream?" without asking the model for any extra numbers.

**Why it was deferred to here.** On the hand-written Hormuz example, almost every arrow has the same backing. The spread would have widened everything equally and taught nothing. Generated maps genuinely mix `documented` and `argued` arrows, so now it means something. On the live run, 8 arrows were documented and 1 was argued. After this change, a map built on sourced mechanisms shows visibly tighter ranges than one built on argument alone.

**The catch.** It changes every computed number. Every number quoted in the spec chapters goes stale at once, so the sweep of those chapters has to travel in the same pull request. That was a hard-won lesson from stack 03.

## 3. The engine carrying the path's multiplied-out likelihood (INV-8)

**What it is.** A causal chain reads persuasively: strait opens, then insurance gets cheaper, then Brent falls. But if each step is 60% likely, the whole chain is about 22%, and stories hide that. Your invariant INV-8 says every path must show its multiplied-out likelihood beside the story, so a convincing narrative can't pass for a likely one.

**Where it stands.** The Inspector's path bar has a slot for this number. When J joined the canvas to the engine, it found that no server route carries the number. Your rule is that the browser never does arithmetic, since a second place that computes numbers is a second engine that will drift. So the slot honestly says "not worked out".

**The work.** It is small. The engine already has the one path-choosing rule, the best-backed route, which M made public for the Verify door. This piece multiplies along that route and puts the result on the world the engine returns. The growing-canvas pull request then shows it.

## 4. The final `ARCHITECTURE.md` and PRD sweep

**What it is.** Your working agreement says `ARCHITECTURE.md` is living: every section is marked *built* or *planned*, and it must match reality. Stack 04 makes a lot of "planned" things real:
- the event stream
- the model boundary
- replay mode
- the recorded-response test layer
- a sixth CI job
- new folders

This pass updates those sections and corrects the test counts. The document says 137 server tests. There are now over 400. It also marks stack 04 done in the PRD's roadmap table and closes the PRD's answered open questions.

**Why it comes last.** It describes both halves, browser and server, so it can only be written truthfully once both are finished. It is documentation only. For a reviewer judging "rigorously documented decisions", this is the page that has to be true.

## 5. The four final recordings

**What it is.** A reviewer who clones the repo with no API key still gets the whole experience. The four example cards on the launchpad play back real recorded generations through the same route, the same stream and the same canvas as a live run. Record 0012 made this a requirement. The four are Hormuz, the midterms, export restrictions on AI models, and photonic chips. For each, the recording also stores one scripted "…but this also happens" intervention.

**Why none exist yet.** A recording is only valid for the exact prompt that produced it. CI fails if a recording's prompt fingerprint doesn't match the current prompt. Recording before the prompt settles means paying to record twice. Your round-two decisions all change the prompt: researched base rates, Sonnet 5, and standalone claim wording. That is why M's prompt round comes first.

**Cost.** Four full generations. On Opus the measured run was $1.32 and 11 minutes for a 10-claim map. Sonnet 5 should be cheaper per token. Your per-claim research budget of up to 25 searches will add to it. I will measure one run first and tell you the real figure before recording all four. Only I run these, with the $15 per-run stop in place.

## How they fit together

Most of this is one last agent's work. Items 1 to 4 go in a single final pull request on the server side, since items 2 and 3 both touch the engine's arithmetic and item 4 documents the result. Item 5 is mine to run and comes at the very end, because the recordings must be made against the final prompt and the final engine. The order is:

1. the prompt round
2. measurement runs
3. that last pull request
4. the four recordings
5. you look at a live map and a replayed one

## Root cause, in two sentences

It reproduced the bug at event 3 of the small run (`C runs into N1: -180 between them`) before the fix. The browser test checks the same thing on the real map from the rendered rectangles.

**A second bug the real run exposed:** the reducer replaced `world.links` with whatever the latest event brought, so a five-claim map was drawn with one arrow. The chapter's run was too small to show it (one arrow per event, and the finished world replaces everything). Arrows now accumulate; `test_every_arrow_that_arrived_is_still_drawn` pins it.

Every claim that **arrives** takes focus (the count is what says one arrived — when the likelihoods land, the engine's world replaces the drawing and its claims come back in map order, which is not an arrival and must not move the view). The view then **brings the tile in only when it is off the edge**, rather than recentring: the promise is that it is on the glass, not in the middle, and recentring on every arrival would yank the map from under somebody reading a tile that was already visible. The lens now only ever reads a claim the map holds, and is off while the map is arriving unless the reader points at something.

That line exists so a reader can ask for this answer again (the map, the seed, the working), and the working is asked for by that name. **5 — the foot said it twice. Fixed.** The live region is now spoken only on this screen (still polite, still read in full); the visible channels are the key line and the origin strip with the `finished` line. Under `width_cap` — the real run — it reads: *"The last line still open was closed because that claim already has every effect one generation draws from it. 10 claims · 9 arrows · 0 refused."* A plain fact, naming the cap and not its value, blaming nobody.

**6 — the launchpad's sentence. Fixed. The wording I chose, for the chapter:**
- All four replayable, all one day → record 0012 word for word: *"No model key configured — these four run from recordings made on 2026-09-18."*
- All four, several days → *"No model key configured — these four run from recordings, the oldest made on 2026-09-18."*
- Some of them → *"No model key configured — one of these four runs from recordings, made on 2026-09-17; the other three have nothing recorded yet."* (counts in words, singular and plural handled, the oldest day named)
- None → nothing is printed.

The field carries the same sentence plus the one thing that is true of it: *"A sentence of your own needs the model, and there is no recording of one."*

**7 — a run that refused nothing. Done.** While the run is going the strip takes no room; the moment it is over it says *"The rules refused nothing in this run."* The real run is the fixture, and the browser test accepts either shape and fails on a silent strip.

**8 — not touched.** `toTwoFigures` and the tile ceiling are untouched; I wrote no height-ceiling test. Ready for the rebase.

Nothing anywhere reads the model's name or length — the strip prints the field and the tests compare against the fixture's own value. The real run's claims are up to 176 characters; they wrap to three lines and stop at a word boundary inside the height the layout was given, which the collision walk checks at every step.

input.message:
Coordinator to J — Kent has asked me to merge stack 04a once its work is done, and an independent read-only reviewer went over #29/#31/#33 first. It found four defects that must be fixed before the merge, all in your branch, plus smaller ones. Same worktree and branch (`feat/04a-join`, tip `f1ef102`); commit on top in small commits, do not rewrite history (G is forked off you), do not push. For each must-fix: write the failing test FIRST, watch it fail, then fix.

**Must fix before merge**
1. **The arrow-number cache is keyed on a branch identity that does not change when the branch changes.** `App.tsx` `wireKey` is `${openId}:${seed}:${linkId}`; `appendEdit` returns a new branch with the same `id`. Start a branch → select `H→B` (conditional cached) → press **This happened** on C: the world and diff are re-asked but the OLD conditional is re-attached and never re-fetched — a number for a branch that no longer exists, with nothing saying so. `App.test.tsx` tests the cache hit, not the invalidation. A branch is append-only, so its edit count (or the wire branch's `interventions.length`) in the key is sufficient and honest — but check: can an edit ever be removed or replaced? If so use something that changes then too.
2. **A branch's conditional is drawn on the map "as it was written", and is fetched for the branch while that map is showing.** `wireKey` ignores `showing`; `paintings.before.links` share ids with the branch's. Open a branch, select an arrow, press Space: the header says *as it was written* and the wire still carries the branch's number; selecting an arrow WHILE showing "before" asks `readConditional` for the branch and paints it on the unedited map. A number on screen belongs to a map the reader is not looking at — a veto. Key and fetch by the map actually showing.
3. **The tile's "no change" badge gives a false reason in the reweighting case.** `graph/diff/branchWorld.ts` ~150–162 says "its likelihood did not move by enough to report". A claim is `unchanged` when the move is under the floor OR the same-direction share is under 90%. Observing C moves H by `.0090` — nearly twice the floor — with a share of exactly 0, and the tile asserts the one thing that is not true of it. The Inspector already has the right sentence for each case; this is one rule written in two places with one copy wrong. One source for the reason, chosen by what the engine's row says (under the floor / versions did not agree / moved only by reweighting). Extend the end-to-end test to read the tile's badge reason in that case.
4. **The Inspector's decomposition lists feedback arrows as pushes.** `Inspector.tsx` ~214 filters `world.links` by target with no `reflexive` test. K1 (binding): anything that asks "what can move" reads the map with feedback arrows set aside. Selecting R shows `B pushes …` — a push that contributed nothing to the number two lines below. The outline already says "Fed back into by"; use the same words, listed apart from the pushes, and say it contributed nothing to this number yet.

**Should fix now, while you are there**
5. `roomFor` (`App.tsx` ~355–366) adds and subtracts already-clamped heights, so it can hand the layout a tile taller than 320 (worked: 320 + 280 − 248 = 352) — reachable on generated maps. Compute the natural height once and clamp once; make `layout.test.ts` call `roomFor` rather than typing heights in.
6. An observation of FALSE would read **Happened** (`apiSource.ts` ~125–132, ~171–183): the `do` path passes the value, the `observe` path does not. Not reachable from today's buttons, reachable from a stored branch. Read `spec/vocabulary.md` for the word an observed-false claim takes; if there is none, tell me and use the plainest true words meanwhile.
7. A conditional that fails once is cached as an absence and never retried, and it says "no engine yet" when the engine was reached and failed (`App.tsx` ~552–565). Do not cache a failure; use the absence kind that is true.
8. `engineState()` mints a new object every render, so the whole branch world is rebuilt on every keystroke — memoise on the answer.
12. `whereItsDaySits` uses an exact `indexOf` where the engine clamps to `[0, days]` — mirror the engine's clamp so a supposed claim never prints the stored `1.0` as `>.99`.
Nits: 13 (`layoutRunner.ts:162` comment names `pinsThatStillHold`; the function is `pinsFor`), 14 (stale comment in `e2e/hormuz.spec.ts` ~206–212 — delete it and assert the whole sentence), 15 (stale "Waiting on the engine fix" in `inspector.test.tsx` ~242), 16 (identity `.map` in `apiSource.ts` ~481), 17 (`DeltaRail.tsx` ~180 prints a raw ISO date where every other day goes through `toDay`), 18 (`spec/workbench/inspector.md` B2 and INV-workbench.54 speak of a `decomposition` field that does not exist — make the chapter say what the code does), 19 (`toSize(0)` prints a bare `0`).
(Findings 9–11 are the engine's and are going to the engine's owner.)

Re-run `npm run check` and `npx playwright test`; re-shoot the states the must-fixes touch (a wire's number before and after an edit; the same arrow on "as it was written"; H's tile after observing C; R selected). Report per item with the failing-then-passing test name, anything you disagree with, and the tails.

content.text:
I'm holding the merge. The two independent reviews you asked for found eight real defects. Neither the roughly 700 tests nor my own review had caught them. All five pull requests were green, and some would still have shipped wrong numbers.

**Must-fix in the join (#33), with J now:**
1. **A stale number that never refreshes.** The number on a wire is cached under the branch's id, and the id stays the same when you add an edit to the branch. Select an arrow, press **This happened** on another claim, and the wire keeps showing the number for a branch that no longer exists.
2. **A number shown on the wrong map.** Toggle to "as it was written" and a selected arrow still carries the branch's number. Select an arrow while that map is showing and the browser fetches the branch's number and paints it on the unedited map.
3. **A false reason on a tile.** In the reweighting case the tile's *no change* badge says the likelihood "did not move by enough". H had moved by nearly twice the floor. The Inspector gives the right reason, so this is one rule written in two places with one copy wrong.
4. **Feedback arrows listed as pushes.** The Inspector lists the feedback arrow into R as a push on R's number. Under your K1 ruling that arrow contributed nothing to it.

**Must-fix in the pipeline (#32), going to M once the recording finishes:**
1. **Concurrent proposals can create a loop.** Three model calls run at once, and each answer is checked against the map as it stood when the round started. Two answers that are each legal alone, A→B and B→A, both get added. The finished map has a loop and no refusal is shown. The reviewer ran this and confirmed it.
2. **Paid-for answers are dropped at the spending cap.** When the cap trips mid-round, answers already paid for never reach the map or the receipt. In the reviewer's run, 7 calls were made and 5 were billed.
3. **The width cap can be bypassed.** An arrow proposal that names a different source claim gets past it. The same arrow can also be added twice, and its push then counts twice in the arithmetic.
4. **An API error loses the whole run.** A rate limit on call 20, for example, discards the map and the receipt.

**One change to the merge plan.**
- The pipeline fixes belong on the stream branch, where those files now live in their latest form. None of them touches the prompt, so the new cassettes stay valid.
- #32 will therefore merge back-to-back with the stream pull request, not on its own ahead of it.
- 04a (#29, then #31, then #33) and the docs pull request (#30) merge as soon as J and F report and I've verified their work.

**Other results from this round:**
- F showed that the zero-strength worry I sent it was wrong. An observation reaches a cause by reweighting the versions of the map, never by travelling along arrows. That held on 900 of 900 maps, even with every arrow flattened to zero, and F pinned it with a named test.
- G fixed the tile collision at its root: a newly arriving box now settles into the first free slot in its column. The no-collision test walks every event of the real 10-claim run. I'll review G's new pictures after J stops.
- M's prompt round is verified, and the Sonnet 5 re-recording is running.

The decision is a 4-branch ladder in `_states`, `diff.py:802-806`:

```python
state: ClaimState = "unchanged"
if _forced_false_in(world_b, claim_id):
    state = "killed"
elif abs(move) >= MOVED_AT_LEAST and agreement >= AGREEING_AT_LEAST:

```

`unchanged` is the *default*: a claim present in both worlds that is not forced false and fails **either** half of the two-part test. Both halves are required.

Constants, `diff.py:104-108`:
- `MOVED_AT_LEAST = 0.005` — "How far a claim has to move before the move counts as a move at all." (the magnitude floor / epsilon)
- `AGREEING_AT_LEAST = 0.90` — "How many of the versions have to move the same way before the move counts." (the consensus requirement)

Inputs to the test, `diff.py:795-801`:
```python
before = world_a.beliefs[claim_id].p
after = world_b.beliefs[claim_id].p
move = after - before
each_version = behind_a.likelihood[claim_id][:, _read_on(world_a, in_a[claim_id])]
each_version_after = behind_b.likelihood[claim_id][:, _read_on(world_b, in_b[claim_id])]
counting = _counting_for(behind_a, behind_b, claim_id)
agreement = _agreement_on(each_version, each_version_after, move, counting)
```
Both numbers are read on the claim's **own resolve-by day** (`_read_on`, `diff.py:575-592`).

Agreement (the "same direction" / worlds-agreeing number) is the weighted share of *paired* per-version differences whose sign matches the reported move — `_agreement_on`, `diff.py:669-671`:
```python
paired = after - before
agreeing = numpy.sign(paired) == numpy.sign(move)
return float((counting * agreeing).sum() / counting.sum())
```

The per-version weights come from `_counting_for`, `diff.py:625-639` — a version counts by the **minimum** of the weights it carried in both worlds, and only for claims inside each world's `reweighted` set (an observation's reach; set from `observation_reach` at `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04a-join/backend/src/katalyst/domain/propagation.py:303,412`), otherwise 1:

in_b = (behind_b.weights if claim_id in behind_b.reweighted else numpy.ones_like(behind_b.weights))
together: Numbers = numpy.minimum(in_a, in_b)
if together.sum() <= 0.0:

```

`unchanged` is the *default*: a claim present in both worlds that is not forced false and fails **either** half of the two-part test. Both halves are required.

Constants, `diff.py:104-108`:
- `MOVED_AT_LEAST = 0.005` — "How far a claim has to move before the move counts as a move at all." (the magnitude floor / epsilon)
- `AGREEING_AT_LEAST = 0.90` — "How many of the versions have to move the same way before the move counts." (the consensus requirement)

Inputs to the test, `diff.py:795-801`:
```python

after = world_b.beliefs[claim_id].p

each_version_after = behind_b.likelihood[claim_id][:, _read_on(world_b, in_b[claim_id])]

Both numbers are read on the claim's **own resolve-by day** (`_read_on`, `diff.py:575-592`).

Coordinator to M — the prompt round verified for me (427 passed; the cache-minimum catch was excellent), and **`make record-cassettes` passed on Sonnet 5: 5 passed in 1 011 s**, key check passed; the four re-recorded cassettes are uncommitted in your worktree. Measured from their usage: 25 searches over 5 calls (2–8 each, never near 25), output 3.5k–12k tokens a call, cache reads 44k–188k, **about $0.19 and about 200 s a call**. A full measurement run (`make run-demo ONLY=hormuz CAP=15`) is running in your worktree in the background right now — it loaded its code at start, so you may edit files, but **do not touch `backend/.runs/` and do not run anything that needs the key**.

Kent asked me to merge the open pull requests, and an independent read-only reviewer went over the pipeline (#32) first. **It found four defects that must be fixed before any of 04b merges** — all CONFIRMED by running. They are structural and none touches the prompt, the shapes or the request body, so **fix them on `feat/04b-stream`, where these files now live** (the cassettes stay valid; #32 and the stream pull request will merge back-to-back). For each: write the failing test FIRST, watch it fail, then fix.

1. **A concurrent round validates every proposal against the map as it stood at the round's START, then folds them all in.** `grow.py` hands one snapshot to all three calls; `expand` checks each against that snapshot; `fold` appends to the running map with no re-check. Map `H→A`, `H→B`, `A→C`; frontier `[H, A, B]`; `A` answers link `A→B`, `B` answers link `B→A`, each legal alone: the finished map holds `A→B→A`, `validate` reports `cycle`, refusals shown: 0. The same hole admits a duplicate claim and a duplicate arrow. **Re-validate where the map actually changes — at the fold, against the map as it then stands** — and a proposal that was legal when asked and is not legal when folded is a refusal like any other (shown, counted, never repaired). Keep the fold order fixed so a run's shape still depends only on its answers.
2. **When the spending cap trips mid-round, answers already paid for are thrown away** — not folded, not yielded, not on the receipt (`grow.py` ~206–210: 7 questions asked, 5 outcomes handed back, `receipt.calls == 5`). `outcome.py`'s own docstring forbids it. Fold and yield every answer in the round, THEN stop. Check your new between-rounds check in `client.py` has the same property: whatever was paid for is counted.
3. **The width cap is only checked on the claim the call was about**, so a `LinkProposal` naming another source walks past it, and the same arrow can be added twice (`H→B` twice; `domain/propagation.py` sums every incoming arrow, so its push counts twice and the canvas draws two wires). Count the width of the ARROW'S OWN source. A second arrow between the same ordered pair of claims: is that a fault in a map? I believe it is and that it belongs in `domain/validity.py` as a violation code with its sentence (you may add it there, with its test and its row in `spec/graph/validity.md` — say "twenty codes" everywhere "nineteen" is said; grep the repo and list every place for me). If you see a reason a map may legitimately hold two arrows between one ordered pair, tell me instead.
4. **Any error from the model call escapes `grow()` and takes the run with it** — no partial map, no receipt, no `Finished`, and the round's other two paid answers dropped unread. A 429 or 529 on call 20 of 40 is ordinary. `Finished`'s docstring promises exactly one, always last. Decide at the seam: a vendor error becomes an outcome of our own that the walk can fold (it counts toward the three in a row like anything that is not an accepted proposal, its plain sentence is shown), the round's other answers are still folded, and a run that cannot continue ends with a `Finished` and the stream's `failed` event carries one plain sentence, never a stack trace. input.message:
Coordinator to M — add this to your current round, at the top. The full measurement run (`make run-demo ONLY=hormuz CAP=15`, Sonnet 5, 26 minutes, paid) **crashed at the end and kept nothing**:

```
    3  accepted  The S&P Global Platts Japan-Korea Marker (JKM) front-month LNG…  (118s)
       so far: 4 calls, $0.73, 21 searches, 2,019 in / 26,749 out (19,710 of it thinking), 10m51s
  drafting the one intervention the card offers: '…but Iran is struck the next day'
    drafted
  File ".../engine/record.py", line 618, in <module>   raise SystemExit(main())
  File ".../engine/record.py", line 263, in run_one    update={"receipt": _with_the_insert(finished.receipt, its_calls)}
NameError: name '_with_the_insert' is not defined
```

**Root cause:** `record.py` has its `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())` guard at line 618 and defines `_with_the_insert` at line 621 — BELOW the guard. Run as a program, `main()` executes before the rest of the module is defined. Imported by a test, everything is defined first, so every test passes and no static check sees it. And because the crash came before the write, `backend/.runs/` has nothing from this run — the second paid run whose receipt is lost, after the fix that was meant to make that impossible.

Fix it at the root, not the symptom:
1. The guard is the last thing in the file — in `record.py` and in every other module with one (`check_recordings.py`, anything else run with `-m`). Add a source-reading test, in the manner of `test_our_own_source.py`: in every module under `src/katalyst`, nothing but blank lines and comments follows the `__main__` guard.
2. **Test the program as a program.** At least one test runs `python -m katalyst.engine.record` (and `check_recordings`) as a subprocess against fake answers — add whatever seam that needs (for instance a setting naming a module whose factory returns the fake answerer, refused unless a test flag is set, or a `--fake` flag that only exists under tests; pick the simplest honest thing and say why) — through the WHOLE path: the generation, the scripted insert, the kept run, the verdict on the recording. It would have caught both this and the earlier `AttributeError` you found at line 601.
3. **"A paid run is never discarded" must survive a crash.** Keep the run incrementally or in a `finally`: the generation's transcript, receipt, map and events are written to `backend/.runs/` as soon as the generation ends and BEFORE the insert is drafted, then updated with the insert; an exception anywhere after the first paid call still leaves a file, with what was spent so far and the exception's one plain sentence in it. Test it with a fake answerer that raises on its Nth call, and with a crash injected after the generation.
4. One observation from this run for later, not for now: with the new prompt the hypothesis's three children were all `market` endings (Brent, TTF, JKM), so the frontier emptied and the map stopped at FOUR claims, depth one — the first-move-jumps-to-a-trade finding is worse, not better. Do not change the prompt in this round (the cassettes were just re-recorded); tell me in your report what you think is causing it and the smallest prompt change you would make, and I will batch it.
Then carry on with the four must-fix defects and the rest.

content.text:
The whole-map Sonnet 5 run failed at the last step, and nothing from it was kept.

**What happened.** The run lasted 26 minutes. The last visible state was 4 calls, $0.73, 21 searches, and 74% of written tokens spent on thinking. It then drafted the scripted "…but Iran is struck" insert and crashed with a `NameError` before writing anything to disk. I've booked it at $2, which puts the total at about $7.90 of $500.

**Why nothing caught it.** The recorder file has its "run me as a program" guard above a function the guard ends up calling. That only breaks when the file is actually run as a program. Every test imports the file, which defines everything first, so all 427 tests passed. Ruff and mypy can't see it either.

**The fix I've told M to make:**
- **The guard goes last in the file.** A test will enforce that for every module.
- **The recorder gets a subprocess test.** It runs as a real program, with fake answers, through the whole path including the insert.
- **A paid run is saved as it goes.** A crash at any point still leaves a file showing what was spent.
- **Handoff.** This is the second time a paid run lost its receipt, so I added it as lesson 16.

**Two things the partial output already shows:**
1. **Pace.** Four claims took about 11 minutes, which is around 2.7 minutes per tile with researched base rates. That matches the 200 seconds per call I measured while recording the cassettes.
2. **A new prompt problem.**
   - **What happened:** the claims are now properly standalone, for example "ICE Brent front-month futures settle at least 8% below…". But all three of the hypothesis's children came back as trades. The frontier emptied, and the map stopped at four claims, one step deep.
   - **What it means:** the rewritten prompt fixed the wording and made the jump-straight-to-a-trade problem worse.
   - **What's next:** I've asked M to diagnose it without touching the prompt, since the cassettes were only just re-recorded. It goes in the next batched round.

Still running: J on the join's must-fix items, and M on the recorder and the pipeline must-fix items. 04a merges as soon as J reports and I've verified it.

**1 — stale conditional cache key.** `wireKey` was `${openId}:${seed}:${linkId}`; `appendEdit` returns a new branch with the same `id`, so after an edit the reader was shown the number worked out before it. Verified the append-only claim before relying on it: `branchReducer.ts` exports four functions, only `appendEdit` touches `edits`, and it appends — no undo, no removal anywhere. The key now carries the edit count.
`test_a_wires_number_is_asked_again_when_the_branch_changes` — failed "called 2 times, but got 1", now passes.

**2 — conditional drawn on the wrong map.** Introduced `shownBranch` (the branch the map in front is drawn from; nothing on "as it was written"). Both the key and the fetch use it.
`test_a_wires_number_belongs_to_the_map_that_is_showing` — same failure, now passes.

**3 — false "no change" reason.** There were **four** copies, each naming a different cause. New `frontend/src/graph/diff/noChange.ts` is the one source; the tile, both rail paths and the panel read it.

**I disagree with one part of this item and did not do it.** You asked the reason be chosen by "under the floor / versions did not agree / moved only by reweighting". The first two cannot be chosen honestly: `MOVED_AT_LEAST = 0.005` and `AGREEING_AT_LEAST = 0.90` live in `backend/src/katalyst/domain/diff.py` and appear nowhere on the wire, so choosing between them means hard-coding the engine's floor and bar in the browser and re-running the `shifted` test — which `branchWorld.ts`'s own docstring and `spec/multiverse/diff.md:392` both forbid. The sentence now gives the verdict, the engine's two readings and the agreement share, and says outright that the engine does not say which half failed. The reweighting case is the exception and is still named, because the engine names it on the row. **Finding for the engine's owner: to say which half failed, the diff needs either the two constants in its answer or a field on the row.**

The live engine confirms the defect was real, not theoretical: on the observe-the-premium branch the talks read `.28` then `.30` with 66% agreement — two points apart — and the old tile told that reader the number "did not move by enough to report".
`test_the_no_change_reason_names_no_cause_the_engine_did_not_give`, `test_the_tile_and_the_rail_give_one_reason_and_not_two`, and e2e step `test_the_tile_says_why_the_engine_reports_no_change`.

**4 — feedback arrows in the decomposition.** Split at the same place the engine splits them. One thing blocks the merge: **`e2e/hormuz.spec.ts` is flaky.** When I ran `npx playwright test` from cold, `the stored example, opened and edited by keyboard alone` failed 2 runs in 5 at line 177 — `opecBefore` was `""` — because it read a chip's `innerText()` once, straight away, before the engine's answer had arrived. I committed a fix on top of your branch (`83e6e6b`: wait with `toHaveText(/^\.\d+$/)` on R's and H's chips before reading). After it: 13 passes and **1 more failure in 14 runs, which I did not capture** — so there is at least one more read-before-ready somewhere in the three tests. Continuous integration is about 2.5× slower than this machine, so a one-in-fourteen flake here is a regular red build there.

Harden all three end-to-end tests at the root: every value the test reads must be WAITED FOR with a web-first assertion (`expect(locator).toHaveText/toContainText/toBeVisible`, or `expect.poll`) before it is read or compared — no bare `innerText()`/`textContent()` on anything that depends on the engine, on layout, on focus moving, or on an announcement; no fixed sleeps. Pay attention to: the numbers after each edit (a new world and a new diff are asked for — the old numbers are still on screen until they arrive, so "wait for a number" is not enough; wait for the thing that CHANGES, e.g. the status line's announcement for that edit, or the branch's name in the header, before reading), the wire's conditional after selection, the flip to "as it was written" and back, and the rail's rows. Then prove it: run `npx playwright test --repeat-each=40` (from cold at least once — stop any dev servers first so Playwright starts both halves itself) and paste the tail. If a run fails, capture which assertion and fix that root too. Same branch, commit on top, do not push. Report the reads you hardened and the tail.

The cause was a counting mistake, not too few worlds: on the Hormuz map, observing that Brent settled below $68 leaves 209 of the 2 000 versions of the map with no surviving world. Such a version counts for nothing in the number and its band, but it still got one vote on which way the number moved, and always voted against — 89.05% same-direction against a 90% bar.

One rule (Kent, 2026-09-17): the direction is read with the same weights the number was read with. It is written once, as Versions.counting_for. Each world falls back on its own before the two are combined, and when no version counted in both numbers there is no direction to report rather than a guessed one. M1 and M2 now read 98.66% and land on the change list; every difference that holds no observation is byte for byte what it was.

A claim moved only by reweighting says so: ClaimDiff gains moved_only_by_reweighting, for a claim with no causes that an observation moves through the version weights alone.

A likelihood is written the same way by the engine and the browser: two significant figures, never an exponent, and a guard word exactly when it is true of the rounded number — below .01 prints <.01, above .99 prints >.99 (Kent, 2026-09-20). A move is not a likelihood and keeps its two figures. A number that is not finite raises instead of printing.

Two property tests now build what they need instead of filtering for it, and one pins that an observation reaches a cause through the version weights even when no arrow pushes.

Both growth events say which claims are still open, so a claim closed by its third refusal loses its rectangle at once, and when the beliefs arrive every rectangle goes. Nothing jumps: a placed tile keeps its position to the pixel and a late arrival finds a gap. Order on screen is causal order, not arrival order: a wire draws only when both its ends exist, and belief chips resolve once, at the end. Every refusal is on screen with the validator's own sentence. The receipt strip prints every field, web searches included, and adds nothing up. No sentence blames the model for our own rules. The canvas is described drawing exactly the Hormuz generation spec/generation/proposals.md writes out step by step. The browser never invents a seed.

Closed in place: the retraction badge comes from the world, not the branch; the receipt and the transcript live in the Inspector; the Inspector shows the whole decomposition or none; an ending that did not move is a greyed "no change" row. The Inspector gains the sentence for a claim moved only by reweighting. "Build the map" and four new on-screen words enter spec/vocabulary.md. The visual review checklist gains a thirteenth line.
